attributes.name: transmission_equipment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.transmission_equipment. Business justification: QoS events trace to specific transmission equipment failures. Critical for NOC rapid incident resolution and equipment health monitoring.

attributes.name: ad_pod_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total duration of the ad pod in seconds when event_type is ad_pod_insertion. Null for other event types.

attributes.name: ad_pod_position
attributes.description: Position of the ad pod within the content stream when event_type is ad_pod_insertion. Null for other event types. Used for DAI analysis.

attributes.name: bitrate_kbps
attributes.description: Current streaming bitrate in kilobits per second at the time of the event. Reflects the ABR profile tier active during this event.

attributes.name: buffer_level_seconds
attributes.description: Amount of video content buffered in the player at the time of the event, measured in seconds. Indicates playback health and risk of stalling.

attributes.name: cdn_cache_status
attributes.description: CDN cache status for the content segment at the time of the event: hit (served from cache), miss (fetched from origin), stale (expired cache), bypass (cache bypassed).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QoS event record was created in the data platform, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used for data lineage and audit purposes.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Type of device on which the playback event occurred: smart TV, mobile phone, tablet, desktop, set-top box, gaming console, etc.

attributes.name: download_throughput_kbps
attributes.description: Measured download throughput in kilobits per second at the time of the event. Used by ABR algorithms to determine optimal bitrate.

attributes.name: drm_system
attributes.description: DRM system protecting the content stream: Widevine, FairPlay, PlayReady, or None for unprotected content.

attributes.name: dropped_frames_count
attributes.description: Number of video frames dropped by the player at the time of the event. Indicates rendering performance issues.

attributes.name: error_code
attributes.description: Specific error code returned by the player or CDN when event_type is error. Null for non-error events. Used for detailed troubleshooting and root-cause analysis.

attributes.name: error_message
attributes.description: Human-readable error message describing the failure when event_type is error. Null for non-error events.

attributes.name: event_severity
attributes.description: Severity level of the QoS event indicating impact on user experience: critical (playback failure), high (significant degradation), medium (noticeable impact), low (minor impact), info (informational only).

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the QoS event occurred during playback, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Type of QoS event captured: buffering start/end, bitrate switch (up/down), error code, stall event, seek event, ad pod insertion signal, or heartbeat. attributes.name: isp_name
attributes.description: Name of the Internet Service Provider through which the viewer is connected. Used for ISP-level QoS analysis and peering optimization.

attributes.name: network_latency_ms
attributes.description: Network round-trip latency in milliseconds measured at the time of the event. Indicates network performance and potential delivery issues.

attributes.name: new_bitrate_kbps
attributes.description: Bitrate in kilobits per second after a bitrate switch event. Populated when event_type is bitrate_switch_up or bitrate_switch_down. Null for other event types.

attributes.name: origin_server_response_time_ms
attributes.description: Response time in milliseconds from the origin server when CDN cache status is miss. Null for cache hits. Indicates origin performance.

attributes.name: playback_position_seconds
attributes.description: Current playback position in seconds within the content at the time of the event. Used to correlate events with specific content segments.

attributes.name: player_state
attributes.description: State of the video player at the time of the event: playing, paused, buffering, seeking, idle, or error.

attributes.name: player_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the video player software that generated this QoS event. Used for player-specific issue analysis.

attributes.name: previous_bitrate_kbps
attributes.description: Bitrate in kilobits per second before a bitrate switch event. Populated when event_type is bitrate_switch_up or bitrate_switch_down. Null for other event types.

attributes.name: seek_position_seconds
attributes.description: Playback position in seconds to which the user seeked. Populated when event_type is seek. Null for other event types.

attributes.name: session_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the parent playback session started, in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Provides temporal context for event sequencing.

attributes.name: stall_duration_ms
attributes.description: Duration of the playback stall or buffering event in milliseconds. Populated when event_type is buffering_start, buffering_end, or stall. Null for other event types.

attributes.name: streaming_protocol
attributes.description: Streaming protocol used for content delivery: HLS (HTTP Live Streaming), MPEG-DASH (Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP), RTMP, WebRTC, or Smooth Streaming.

attributes.name: user_agent
attributes.description: User agent string of the viewer device and browser/app at the time of the event. Used for device and platform-specific issue analysis.

attributes.name: viewer_ip_address
attributes.description: IP address of the viewer device at the time of the event. Used for network-level troubleshooting and geographic analysis. May be considered PII in some jurisdictions.

Used for SLA performance tracking and breach alerting.

attributes.name: breach_penalty_type

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: critical_threshold
attributes.description: The threshold value at which a critical alert is triggered, indicating an SLA breach has occurred or is imminent.

attributes.name: data_source

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this SLA definition becomes active and enforceable.

attributes.name: escalation_procedure
attributes.description: Description of the escalation process and contacts when an SLA breach occurs or is imminent.

attributes.name: exclusion_criteria
attributes.description: Conditions or events that are excluded from SLA measurement (e.g., scheduled maintenance, force majeure, third-party failures).

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: The geographic region or market to which this SLA applies (e.g., 'Global', 'North America', 'EMEA', 'APAC').

attributes.name: measurement_frequency
attributes.description: How often the metric is sampled and evaluated (real-time, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly).

attributes.name: measurement_window
attributes.description: The time period over which the SLA metric is calculated and evaluated (e.g., 'monthly', 'daily', 'rolling_30_days', 'per_incident').

attributes.name: metric_name
attributes.description: Name of the specific performance metric being measured (e.g., 'Streaming Uptime', 'Start Time Latency', 'Rebuffering Ratio', 'CDN Cache Hit Rate', 'DRM License Issuance Latency', 'API Response Time').

attributes.name: metric_type
attributes.description: Classification of the metric being measured (uptime, latency, throughput, error rate, response time, availability).

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SLA definition record was last modified.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or operational guidance related to this SLA definition.

attributes.name: owner_department
attributes.description: The business department or team responsible for managing and enforcing this SLA (e.g., 'Platform Operations', 'Distribution', 'Customer Success').

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: How often SLA performance reports are generated and delivered to stakeholders (real-time, daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly).

attributes.name: service_tier
attributes.description: The subscription or service tier to which this SLA applies (premium, standard, basic, enterprise).

attributes.name: sla_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code for the SLA definition used in contracts and operational systems.

attributes.name: sla_definition_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the SLA, including business context, objectives, and any special conditions.

attributes.name: sla_definition_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the SLA definition (active, inactive, draft, superseded, retired).

attributes.name: sla_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the SLA definition (e.g., 'Premium Streaming Uptime SLA', 'Standard CDN Performance SLA').

attributes.name: sla_type
attributes.description: Category of SLA defining the nature of the service commitment (availability, performance, quality, capacity, support, security).

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The target threshold value that defines the SLA commitment (e.g., 99.9 for 99.9% uptime, 2.0 for 2 seconds latency).

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit in which the metric is measured (e.g., 'percent', 'milliseconds', 'seconds', 'requests_per_second', 'ratio').

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for this SLA definition, used to track revisions and changes over time.

attributes.name: warning_threshold
attributes.description: The threshold value at which a warning alert is triggered, indicating performance is approaching but has not yet breached the SLA target.

products.name: sla_performance
products.description: Transactional records tracking actual SLA performance measurements against defined SLA targets over time. Captures SLA definition reference, measurement period (hourly/daily/monthly), actual metric value, target value, breach flag, breach severity, affected platform/region, root-cause category, remediation action taken, and sign-off status. Distinct from sla_definition (the target) — this is the operational record of measured performance. Supports SLA reporting to distribution partners and internal governance.

attributes.name: sla_performance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the SLA performance measurement record.

attributes.name: broadcast_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.broadcast_facility. Business justification: SLA measurements are facility-specific for uptime and latency reporting. Required for facility-level SLA compliance reporting and vendor performance reviews.

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.market_coverage. Business justification: SLA measurement is market-specific due to CDN topology, regional infrastructure differences, and DMA-level service commitments in distribution partner agreements. Required for carriage fee penalty cal

attributes.name: penalty_credit_memo_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.credit_memo. Business justification: SLA breaches trigger contractual penalties and service credits to distribution partners or advertisers. Real business process: SLA penalty assessment, makegood credit issuance, partner compensation fo

attributes.name: sla_definition_id
attributes.description: Reference to the SLA definition that establishes the target thresholds and measurement criteria for this performance record.

attributes.name: tech_incident_id
attributes.description: The identifier of the incident management ticket or case associated with this SLA breach. Links to operational incident tracking systems.

attributes.name: actual_value
attributes.description: The actual measured value of the SLA metric during the measurement period. Unit of measure is defined in the associated SLA definition.

attributes.name: affected_platform
attributes.description: The distribution platform affected by this SLA measurement (e.g., OTT streaming, linear broadcast, MVPD carriage, FAST channel, CDN endpoint). Identifies the delivery channel scope.

attributes.name: affected_region
attributes.description: The geographic region or market affected by this SLA measurement. May be a country code, region name, or CDN edge location identifier.

attributes.name: breach_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The total duration in minutes that the SLA was in breach state during the measurement period. Null if no breach occurred.

attributes.name: breach_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the SLA was breached during this measurement period. True indicates a breach occurred; False indicates SLA was met.

attributes.name: breach_severity
attributes.description: The severity classification of the SLA breach if one occurred. None indicates no breach; minor through critical indicate escalating severity levels based on business impact.

attributes.name: cdn_provider
attributes.description: The CDN provider responsible for content delivery during this measurement period (e.g., Akamai, Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront). Relevant for streaming and OTT SLA measurements.

attributes.name: contract_reference
attributes.description: The contract or agreement reference number under which this SLA is defined. Links performance measurement to contractual obligations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this SLA performance record was first created in the system. Part of audit trail for data lineage.

attributes.name: device_category
attributes.description: The category of end-user device for which this SLA performance was measured (e.g., smart TV, mobile, desktop, set-top box, gaming console). Relevant for device-specific QoS monitoring.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this SLA performance measurement is under dispute by the distribution partner or internal stakeholders. True indicates active dispute.

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Textual description of the reason for disputing this SLA performance measurement. Captures partner or stakeholder objections for resolution tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this SLA performance record was last modified. Tracks updates through validation, dispute, and approval workflows.

attributes.name: measurement_granularity
attributes.description: The time granularity at which this SLA performance measurement was captured (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual).

attributes.name: measurement_period_end
attributes.description: The end timestamp of the measurement period for this SLA performance record. Represents the conclusion of the observation window.

attributes.name: measurement_period_start
attributes.description: The start timestamp of the measurement period for this SLA performance record. Represents the beginning of the observation window.

attributes.name: measurement_source
attributes.description: The source system or monitoring tool that captured this SLA performance measurement (e.g., Akamai CDN analytics, Ericsson MediaFirst monitoring, custom QoS probe). Provides data lineage.

attributes.name: measurement_status
attributes.description: The workflow status of this SLA performance measurement record. Tracks progression from initial capture through validation, dispute resolution, and final approval.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form notes providing additional context, operational commentary, or special circumstances related to this SLA performance measurement.

attributes.name: partner_name
attributes.description: The name of the distribution partner (MVPD, vMVPD, OTT platform, syndication partner) to whom this SLA applies. Used for partner-specific SLA reporting and governance.

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: The monetary penalty or service credit amount assessed due to the SLA breach. Expressed in the contract currency. Null if no penalty applies.

attributes.name: penalty_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether a contractual penalty or service credit is applicable due to this SLA breach. True indicates financial or contractual consequences apply.

attributes.name: penalty_currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the penalty amount (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR).

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Description of the corrective action taken to address the SLA breach or performance degradation. Documents operational response and resolution steps.

attributes.name: remediation_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when remediation action was completed and normal service levels were restored. Null if remediation is pending or not applicable.

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: The high-level category of the root cause for SLA breach or performance degradation (e.g., network congestion, origin server failure, CDN capacity, encoding issue, third-party dependency). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: network|infrastructure|capacity|configuration|third-party|content|security|unknown — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed textual description of the root cause analysis findings for the SLA breach or performance issue. Provides operational context for remediation and reporting.

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: The number of individual observations or data points used to calculate the aggregated SLA metric value. Provides statistical context for measurement confidence.

attributes.name: streaming_protocol
attributes.description: The streaming protocol used for content delivery during this measurement (HLS, MPEG-DASH, RTMP, WebRTC, Smooth Streaming). Applicable to OTT and streaming SLA measurements.

attributes.name: target_value
attributes.description: The target value defined in the SLA definition that the actual performance is measured against. Represents the contractual or operational commitment.

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: The threshold value at which an SLA breach is triggered. May differ from target value to allow for acceptable variance before breach declaration.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit of measure for the SLA metric values (e.g., milliseconds, percentage, Mbps, count, ratio). Provides context for interpreting actual, target, and threshold values.

attributes.name: validated_by
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the user who validated this SLA performance measurement. Part of the approval and sign-off workflow.

attributes.name: validated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this SLA performance measurement was validated and approved. Null if validation is pending.

attributes.name: variance_percentage
attributes.description: The variance expressed as a percentage of the target value. Calculated as ((actual - target) / target) * 100.

attributes.name: variance_value
attributes.description: The calculated variance between actual value and target value (actual minus target). Positive values indicate over-performance, negative values indicate under-performance.

products.name: api_endpoint
products.description: Master registry of all business-facing API endpoints exposed by the OTT platform — content discovery, playback authorization, subscriber entitlement, EPG, search, recommendation, and DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) APIs. Captures endpoint path, HTTP method, API version, authentication scheme (OAuth2, API key, JWT), rate limit policy, SLA tier, deprecation date, owning service, and documentation URL. Distinct from streaming_endpoint (media delivery) — this governs the application API surface.

attributes.name: api_endpoint_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the API endpoint. Primary key.

attributes.name: broadcast_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.broadcast_facility. Business justification: API endpoints are hosted in specific facilities for disaster recovery and data residency compliance. Critical for DR planning and API geographic latency optimization.

attributes.name: compliance_consent_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.consent_record. Business justification: API endpoints accessing subscriber data must validate consent scope before processing. Endpoint authorization checks consent records in real-time to enforce GDPR, CCPA, and privacy policy requirements

attributes.name: noc_monitor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.noc_monitor. Business justification: API endpoints require NOC monitoring for availability. Required for API monitoring setup and SLA compliance measurement.

attributes.name: ott_platform_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.ott_platform. Business justification: API endpoints are exposed by specific OTT platforms. Each API belongs to a platform service. Essential for API governance and platform-specific routing.

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: API endpoints require engineering ownership for deprecation decisions, rate limit adjustments, SLA monitoring, and breaking change management. Essential for on-call rotations, API versioning accountab

attributes.name: tech_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.tech_project. Business justification: API endpoints are developed via technology projects. Required for API development project tracking and feature release management.

attributes.name: tech_sla_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.tech_sla. Business justification: API endpoints have technology SLAs for availability and response time. Required for API SLA compliance tracking and performance optimization.

attributes.name: activated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this endpoint was activated and made available for use. Null if the endpoint has never been activated or is still in development.

attributes.name: allowed_origins
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of allowed origin domains for CORS requests (e.g., https://www.example.com, https://app.example.com). Asterisk (*) indicates all origins are allowed. Null if CORS is disabled.

attributes.name: api_version
attributes.description: The version of the API that this endpoint belongs to (e.g., v1, v2, v3). Used for versioning and backward compatibility management.

attributes.name: authentication_scheme
attributes.description: The authentication mechanism required to access this endpoint (OAuth2 for token-based, API key for simple key-based, JWT for JSON Web Token, basic auth for username/password, none for public endpoints).

attributes.name: authorization_scope
attributes.description: The OAuth2 scope or permission level required to access this endpoint (e.g., read:content, write:profile, admin:all). Defines what actions the authenticated user is authorized to perform.

attributes.name: cache_strategy
attributes.description: The caching strategy applied to responses from this endpoint (no_cache for dynamic data, private for user-specific data, public for shared data, cdn for CDN-cacheable content).

attributes.name: cache_ttl_seconds
attributes.description: The time-to-live in seconds for cached responses from this endpoint. Defines how long the response can be cached before it must be revalidated. Null indicates no caching.

attributes.name: cors_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether Cross-Origin Resource Sharing is enabled for this endpoint (true), allowing web browsers to make requests from different domains, or disabled (false) for same-origin only.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this API endpoint record was first created in the registry. Used for audit trail and lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: deprecation_date
attributes.description: The date when this endpoint was officially marked as deprecated. Used to track the deprecation timeline and communicate sunset schedules to API consumers.

attributes.name: documentation_url
attributes.description: The URL to the detailed API documentation for this endpoint, typically hosted in a developer portal or API documentation system (e.g., Swagger, Postman, Confluence).

attributes.name: endpoint_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the endpoint's purpose, functionality, and business use case. Explains what the endpoint does and when it should be used.

attributes.name: endpoint_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label for the API endpoint (e.g., Content Search, Playback Authorization, Subscriber Entitlement Check).

attributes.name: endpoint_path
attributes.description: The URI path of the API endpoint (e.g., /api/v2/content/search, /api/v1/playback/authorize). This is the resource path exposed to API consumers.

attributes.name: endpoint_status
attributes.description: The current operational status of the endpoint (active for production use, beta for testing with select partners, alpha for internal testing, inactive for disabled, maintenance for temporary unavailability).

attributes.name: functional_category
attributes.description: The business function or domain that this endpoint serves (e.g., content discovery for browsing, playback authorization for DRM, DAI for Dynamic Ad Insertion, EPG for Electronic Program Guide). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: content_discovery|playback_authorization|subscriber_entitlement|epg|search|recommendation|dai|user_profile|analytics|billing — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: http_method
attributes.description: The HTTP method supported by this endpoint (GET for retrieval, POST for creation, PUT for full update, PATCH for partial update, DELETE for removal). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|HEAD|OPTIONS — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: is_deprecated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this endpoint has been marked as deprecated (true) and should no longer be used by new integrations. Deprecated endpoints are maintained for backward compatibility but will eventually be removed.

attributes.name: is_public
attributes.description: Indicates whether this endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication (true) or requires authentication (false). Public endpoints are typically used for content discovery and marketing.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this API endpoint record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: owning_service
attributes.description: The name of the microservice or backend service that implements and owns this endpoint (e.g., content-service, playback-service, subscriber-service). Used for operational ownership and incident routing.

attributes.name: owning_team
attributes.description: The engineering team responsible for maintaining and supporting this endpoint (e.g., Content Platform Team, Playback Engineering, Subscriber Services). Used for escalation and change management.

attributes.name: rate_limit_requests_per_day
attributes.description: The maximum number of requests allowed per day for this endpoint under the assigned rate limit tier. Used for daily quota enforcement.

attributes.name: rate_limit_requests_per_minute
attributes.description: The maximum number of requests allowed per minute for this endpoint under the assigned rate limit tier. Null indicates no specific limit or unlimited access.

attributes.name: rate_limit_tier
attributes.description: The rate limiting tier applied to this endpoint, determining how many requests per time window are allowed (e.g., public tier allows 100 req/min, enterprise allows 10000 req/min).

attributes.name: replacement_endpoint_path
attributes.description: The URI path of the replacement endpoint that should be used instead of this deprecated endpoint. Null if no direct replacement exists. Used to guide API consumers during migration.

attributes.name: request_content_type
attributes.description: The expected content type for the request body (e.g., application/json for JSON payloads, application/xml for XML). Null for endpoints that do not accept a request body (e.g., GET requests).

attributes.name: response_content_type
attributes.description: The content type returned by this endpoint in the response body (e.g., application/json for JSON responses, application/xml for XML). Defines the format of the data returned to the client.

attributes.name: sla_response_time_ms
attributes.business_glossary_term: SLA (Service Level Agreement) Response Time Milliseconds
attributes.description: The target response time in milliseconds for this endpoint under normal load conditions (e.g., 200ms for p95, 500ms for p99). Used for performance monitoring and alerting.

attributes.name: sla_tier
attributes.description: The service level agreement tier for this endpoint, defining uptime guarantees, response time targets, and support priority (e.g., mission_critical requires 99.99% uptime, gold requires 99.9%).

attributes.name: sla_uptime_percentage
attributes.description: The guaranteed uptime percentage for this endpoint as defined in the SLA (e.g., 99.99 for four nines, 99.9 for three nines). Measured monthly.

attributes.name: sunset_date
attributes.description: The planned date when this endpoint will be permanently removed and no longer available. Null if no sunset is planned. Used to give API consumers advance notice for migration.

attributes.name: supports_filtering
attributes.description: Indicates whether this endpoint supports query parameter filtering to narrow down results (true) or returns a fixed result set (false). Filtering allows clients to request specific subsets of data.

attributes.name: supports_pagination
attributes.description: Indicates whether this endpoint supports pagination for large result sets (true) or returns all results in a single response (false). Paginated endpoints typically accept page and page_size query parameters.

attributes.name: supports_sorting
attributes.description: Indicates whether this endpoint supports query parameter sorting to order results (true) or returns results in a default order (false). Sorting allows clients to control result ordering.

products.name: personalization_engine
products.description: Master configuration record for each personalization and recommendation engine instance deployed on the OTT platform (Adobe Experience Platform integration). Captures engine name, algorithm type (collaborative filtering, content-based, hybrid), model version, training data window, feature set configuration, A/B test variant assignment, target platform, refresh cadence, cold-start strategy, and operational status. SSOT for the personalization layer configuration distinct from individual recommendation events.

attributes.name: personalization_engine_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the personalization engine instance. Primary key for the personalization engine configuration record.

attributes.name: compliance_consent_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.consent_record. Business justification: Personalization engines processing user data must validate consent before profiling. Engine operations are gated by consent status for analytics, personalization, and third-party sharing.

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.demographic_segment. Business justification: Recommendation algorithms incorporate demographic signals for content discovery, cold-start personalization, and Nielsen-aligned performance prediction. Supports demographic-based A/B testing and enga

attributes.name: fallback_engine_personalization_engine_id
attributes.description: Reference to an alternative personalization engine to use if this engine fails or returns insufficient recommendations. Ensures continuous user experience during engine failures or maintenance.

attributes.name: ott_platform_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.ott_platform. Business justification: Personalization engines are deployed per OTT platform. Each engine instance serves a specific platform. Removes target_platform STRING (derivable from ott_platform).

attributes.name: owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Personalization engines require data science/ML engineering ownership for model training, A/B test analysis, performance monitoring, and GDPR/CCPA compliance. Essential for accountability in recommend

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.audience_segment. Business justification: Modern personalization relies on behavioral segments for recommendation accuracy and engagement optimization. Supports genre affinity modeling, viewing pattern analysis, and cross-platform content dis

attributes.name: software_license_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.software_license. Business justification: Personalization engines use licensed ML frameworks. Required for ML software license compliance and engine cost allocation.

attributes.name: tech_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.tech_project. Business justification: Personalization engines are deployed via ML projects. Required for personalization project ROI tracking and model deployment timeline management.

attributes.name: ab_test_variant
attributes.description: A/B test variant identifier if this engine is part of an experimentation framework (e.g., 'control', 'variant_a', 'variant_b'). Null if not part of active testing.

attributes.name: algorithm_type
attributes.description: The machine learning algorithm type used by the personalization engine. Collaborative filtering uses user behavior patterns, content-based uses content attributes, hybrid combines both approaches, matrix factorization decomposes user-item interactions, deep learning uses neural networks, and contextual bandit balances exploration and exploitation.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform - ML Algorithm Standards

attributes.name: api_endpoint_url
attributes.description: Uniform Resource Locator (URL) of the Application Programming Interface (API) endpoint that serves recommendations from this engine. Used by client applications to request personalized content.

attributes.name: business_justification
attributes.description: Business rationale and expected outcomes for deploying this personalization engine (e.g., 'Increase Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) by 15%', 'Reduce churn rate by improving content discovery', 'Support new FAST channel launch').

attributes.name: cache_ttl_seconds
attributes.description: Time-To-Live (TTL) in seconds for cached recommendations. Balances recommendation freshness against system performance. Shorter TTL provides more current recommendations but increases computational load.

attributes.name: ccpa_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this personalization engine complies with California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) requirements, including opt-out mechanisms and data sale restrictions.

attributes.name: cold_start_strategy
attributes.description: Strategy used to generate recommendations for new users or content with insufficient interaction history. Popularity-based shows trending content, content similarity uses metadata matching, demographic default uses segment averages, hybrid fallback combines multiple approaches, and random exploration introduces serendipity.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform - Cold Start Handling

attributes.name: confidence_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum confidence score (0.00 to 1.00) required for a recommendation to be surfaced to users. Lower thresholds increase recommendation volume but may reduce relevance.

attributes.name: content_filter_rules
attributes.description: Business rules defining content eligibility for recommendations (e.g., exclude expired rights, enforce parental controls, respect geographic blackouts, honor windowing restrictions). Stored as structured text or JSON.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this personalization engine configuration record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: deployment_date
attributes.description: Date when this personalization engine instance was first deployed to production. Used for tracking engine age and performance trends over time.

attributes.name: diversity_threshold
attributes.description: Minimum diversity score (0.00 to 1.00) enforced in recommendation sets to prevent filter bubbles. Higher values ensure greater variety in content genres, formats, and themes.

attributes.name: engine_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier code for the personalization engine (e.g., 'HOME_REC_01', 'CONT_DISC_02'). Used for system integration and API references.

attributes.name: engine_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the personalization engine instance (e.g., 'Homepage Recommender', 'Content Discovery Engine', 'Next Episode Predictor'). Used for operational identification and reporting.

attributes.name: feature_set_configuration
attributes.description: JSON or structured text describing the feature set used by the model (e.g., viewing history, genre preferences, time-of-day patterns, device type, engagement metrics). Defines the input variables for the recommendation algorithm.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform - Feature Engineering Standards

attributes.name: gdpr_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this personalization engine complies with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requirements for audience data processing, including consent management, data minimization, and right to erasure.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 25 - Data Protection by Design

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this personalization engine configuration record. Critical for change tracking and configuration management.

attributes.name: last_training_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent model training execution. Critical for monitoring model freshness and ensuring recommendations reflect current user behavior patterns.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the deployed machine learning model (e.g., 'v1.2.3'). Follows semantic versioning convention for model lifecycle management and rollback capability.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform - Model Versioning Standard

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the personalization engine. Active engines serve live traffic, inactive are disabled, testing are in validation phase, deprecated are scheduled for retirement, and maintenance indicates temporary unavailability.

attributes.name: owner_team
attributes.description: Name of the business or technical team responsible for this personalization engine instance. Used for operational accountability and incident escalation.

attributes.name: performance_metric_target
attributes.description: Primary business metric this personalization engine is optimized to maximize. Click-through rate measures initial engagement, watch time measures sustained viewing, completion rate measures content finish rate, engagement score is a composite metric, and revenue per user measures monetization impact.

attributes.name: personalization_scope
attributes.description: Granularity level at which personalization is applied. User-level provides individual recommendations, segment-level groups similar users, household-level considers shared viewing, and device-level adapts to device context.

attributes.name: recommendation_count_limit
attributes.description: Maximum number of recommendations this engine will return per request. Typical values range from 10 to 100 depending on user interface requirements and performance constraints.

attributes.name: refresh_cadence
attributes.description: Frequency at which the personalization model is retrained or recommendations are regenerated. Real-time engines update continuously, while batch engines refresh on schedule.

attributes.name: response_time_sla_ms
attributes.business_glossary_term: Response Time Service Level Agreement (SLA) Milliseconds
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable response time in milliseconds for recommendation requests as defined in the Service Level Agreement (SLA). Typical values range from 100ms to 500ms for real-time engines.

attributes.name: training_data_window_days
attributes.description: Number of days of historical data used to train the personalization model. Typical values range from 30 to 365 days depending on content velocity and user behavior patterns.

products.name: dai_configuration
products.description: Configuration records for Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI) on the OTT platform — defining ad pod placement rules, SCTE-35 signal handling, ad decision server (ADS) endpoints, fill-rate fallback logic, ad stitching mode (server-side vs client-side), blackout override rules, and frequency cap enforcement. Captures DAI config name, applicable content type (VOD, live), ad server URL, timeout thresholds, and effective date. Bridges the platform domain with the advertising domain's campaign delivery.

attributes.name: dai_configuration_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the DAI configuration record. Primary key.

attributes.name: configuration_owner_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: DAI configurations control ad insertion logic and revenue streams, requiring ownership for approval workflows, fill rate troubleshooting, blackout override decisions, and ad server contract compliance

attributes.name: ott_platform_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.ott_platform. Business justification: DAI configurations are platform-specific. Each DAI config applies to a specific OTT platform for ad insertion rules and targeting.

attributes.name: abr_profile_compatibility
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of ABR streaming profiles this DAI configuration is compatible with (e.g., HLS, MPEG-DASH, Smooth Streaming).

attributes.name: ad_decision_server_url
attributes.description: Endpoint URL for the Ad Decision Server that determines which ads to serve based on targeting criteria and inventory availability.

attributes.name: ad_format_support
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of supported ad formats for this configuration (e.g., VAST, VMAP, VPAID, SIMID).

attributes.name: ad_pod_placement_rules
attributes.description: Business rules defining where ad pods (groups of ads in a break) can be inserted within the content, including pre-roll, mid-roll, and post-roll positions.

attributes.name: ad_server_timeout_milliseconds
attributes.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for a response from the ad decision server before triggering fallback logic.

attributes.name: backup_ad_server_url
attributes.description: Failover endpoint URL for ad decision requests when the primary ad server is unavailable or times out.

attributes.name: blackout_override_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether this DAI configuration can override geographic blackout restrictions for ad insertion purposes.

attributes.name: cdn_integration_mode
attributes.description: How the DAI system integrates with the CDN: direct (CDN serves pre-stitched streams), proxied (DAI proxies through CDN), or edge decisioning (ad decisions at CDN edge).

attributes.name: companion_ads_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether companion banner ads are displayed alongside video ads to enhance engagement and click-through rates.

attributes.name: configuration_code

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: cdn_provider
attributes.description: The CDN provider responsible for content delivery at the time of the breach, used for vendor accountability.

attributes.name: contract_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the contract or service agreement under which the SLA commitment was made, used for dispute resolution.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this breach record was first created in the system for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: detection_method
attributes.description: The method by which the SLA breach was detected, indicating whether it was proactive monitoring or reactive reporting.

attributes.name: dispute_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the breach determination or penalty is under dispute by the partner or service provider.

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Explanation provided for disputing the breach determination, penalty calculation, or responsibility assignment.

attributes.name: escalation_level
attributes.description: The escalation tier reached during breach resolution, indicating the organizational level involved in remediation.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this breach record was last updated, tracking changes throughout the breach lifecycle.

attributes.name: makegood_triggered_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a makegood (compensatory delivery or ad spot) was triggered as a result of this breach.

attributes.name: measured_value
attributes.description: The actual measured value of the metric at the time of breach, representing the performance level that violated the SLA threshold.

attributes.name: metric_name
attributes.description: The specific SLA metric that was breached, such as uptime percentage, latency, error rate, or availability.

attributes.name: metric_type
attributes.description: Category of the SLA metric that was breached, classifying the nature of the performance issue.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes or comments regarding the breach, investigation, or resolution for operational context.

attributes.name: notification_sent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether breach notification was sent to affected partners, stakeholders, or customers as required by SLA terms.

attributes.name: notification_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when breach notification was sent to affected parties.

attributes.name: partner_name
attributes.description: The name of the distribution partner or MVPD affected by the breach, relevant for partner SLA reporting.

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: The monetary penalty or service credit amount triggered by the breach, as defined in the SLA contract.

attributes.name: penalty_applicable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a contractual penalty or credit is applicable for this breach based on SLA terms.

attributes.name: penalty_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the penalty amount.

attributes.name: remediation_action
attributes.description: Description of the corrective action taken to resolve the breach and restore service to acceptable levels.

attributes.name: resolution_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the breach was resolved and service was restored to within SLA parameters.

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level categorization of the underlying cause of the SLA breach, used for trend analysis and preventive action.

attributes.name: root_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative explanation of the root cause identified through investigation, providing context for the breach.

attributes.name: streaming_protocol
attributes.description: The streaming protocol in use when the breach occurred, such as HLS or MPEG-DASH.

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: The SLA threshold value that was violated, representing the minimum acceptable performance level defined in the SLA commitment.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: The unit in which the metric is measured, such as percentage, milliseconds, Mbps, or requests per second.

attributes.name: validated_by
attributes.description: The user or system that validated the breach measurement and determination, ensuring accuracy for reporting.

attributes.name: validated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the breach record was validated and approved for reporting or penalty processing.

attributes.name: variance_percentage
attributes.description: The variance expressed as a percentage of the threshold, providing a normalized measure of breach severity.

attributes.name: variance_value
attributes.description: The calculated difference between the measured value and the threshold value, quantifying the magnitude of the breach.

products.name: dai_session
products.description: Transactional record capturing Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI) sessions executed during streaming delivery. Captures session identifier, delivery channel or stream, viewer session reference, ad pod position (pre-roll, mid-roll, post-roll), SCTE-35 signal timestamp, ad decision server response, number of ads inserted, fill rate, fallback ad flag, and DAI provider (e.g., Google DAI, Yospace). Supports AVOD and FAST channel monetization reconciliation and ad fill rate optimization.
products.reference: DAI Session / SCTE-35 Ad Insertion Event

attributes.name: dai_session_id

attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST)

attributes.name: ad_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to advertising.ad_order. Business justification: DAI sessions fulfill contracted ad orders. Linking to ad_order enables order-level delivery tracking, contracted-vs-actual reconciliation, billing verification, and order fulfillment reporting. Essent

attributes.name: campaign_id

attributes.name: channel_id

attributes.name: content_rating_id

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.demographic_segment. Essential for upfront commitment fulfillment and Nielsen-rated commerci

attributes.name: media_asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the content asset (video, live stream, FAST channel) being delivered when the DAI session was executed.

attributes.name: playback_session_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent streaming playback session during which this DAI session occurred. Links DAI monetization events to viewer streaming activity.
attributes.references: SCTE-35 Digital Program Insertion Cueing Message

attributes.name: political_ad_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.political_ad_record. Business justification: DAI sessions inserting political ads must create political ad records for FCC public inspection files. Real-time ad insertion generates compliance documentation including sponsor identification and ra

attributes.name: revenue_stream_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.revenue_stream. Business justification: DAI (dynamic ad insertion) sessions generate advertising revenue streams. Daily ad revenue reconciliation ties DAI sessions to revenue streams for accrual accounting and reconciliation with ad server

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.audience_segment. Business justification: Behavioral audience segments enable advanced programmatic targeting beyond demographics, supporting lookalike modeling, cross-platform campaign optimization, and addressable advertising in modern ad t

attributes.name: streaming_endpoint_id
attributes.description: Reference to the streaming endpoint (CDN edge, origin server) that served the DAI-enabled stream.
attributes.references: SCTE-224 Event Scheduling and Notification Interface

attributes.name: subscriber_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the subscriber or viewer associated with this DAI session. Enables personalized ad targeting and frequency capping.

attributes.name: talent_profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to talent.talent_profile. Business justification: Backend gross participation clauses in talent contracts require tracking ad revenue generated during content delivery featuring specific talent. Broadcasters must link dynamic ad insertion sessions to

attributes.name: ad_decision_server_response_time_ms
attributes.business_glossary_term: Ad Decision Server Response Time in Milliseconds
attributes.description: Time in milliseconds taken by the ad decision server to respond with ad selection. Critical for measuring DAI latency and QoS.

attributes.name: ad_decision_server_url
attributes.business_glossary_term: Ad Decision Server Uniform Resource Locator (URL)
attributes.description: URL of the ad decision server (ADS) that was queried to determine which ads to insert. Typically a VAST or VMAP endpoint.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) 4.2

attributes.name: ad_pod_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total duration of the ad pod in seconds. Represents the available inventory window for ad insertion.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST)

attributes.name: ad_pod_position
attributes.description: Position of the ad pod within the content stream. Indicates whether ads were served before content (pre-roll), during content (mid-roll), or after content (post-roll).
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST) 4.2

attributes.name: ad_pod_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential number of this ad pod within the content playback session. Enables tracking of multiple ad breaks within a single viewing session.

attributes.name: ad_targeting_segment_ids
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of audience segment IDs applied for ad targeting during this DAI session. Links to audience segmentation and personalization strategies.

attributes.name: ads_fallback_count
attributes.description: Number of fallback or house ads served when primary ad inventory was unavailable. Indicates unfilled demand.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST)

attributes.name: ads_inserted_count
attributes.description: Number of ads successfully inserted and delivered during this DAI session. Used to calculate fill rate and monetization efficiency.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST)

attributes.name: ads_requested_count
attributes.description: Number of ad slots requested from the ad decision server for this DAI session. Represents the maximum fill capacity of the ad pod.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST)

attributes.name: app_version
attributes.description: Version of the streaming application or player that executed the DAI session. Used for troubleshooting and feature compatibility analysis.

attributes.name: blackout_override_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether geographic blackout restrictions were overridden for this DAI session. True if blackout rules were bypassed (e.g., for authenticated subscribers).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DAI session record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Type of device on which the DAI session was delivered. Influences ad format compatibility and targeting strategies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: smart_tv|mobile|tablet|desktop|set_top_box|gaming_console|streaming_stick|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: drm_enforcement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether DRM protection was enforced on the ad-stitched stream. True if ads were delivered with DRM encryption.

attributes.name: error_code
attributes.description: Error code returned if the DAI session encountered a failure. Used for troubleshooting ad delivery issues and optimizing fill rates.

attributes.name: error_message
attributes.description: Human-readable error message describing the failure reason if the DAI session did not complete successfully.

attributes.name: fill_rate_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of requested ad slots that were successfully filled with paid ads. Calculated as (ads_inserted_count / ads_requested_count) * 100. Key monetization metric.

attributes.name: frequency_cap_applied_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether frequency capping rules were applied to limit ad repetition for this viewer. True if frequency cap was enforced.

attributes.name: geographic_country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO country code representing the viewers geographic location. Derived from IP address or device GPS. Used for geo-targeted ad campaigns.

attributes.name: geographic_dma_code
attributes.description: Nielsen Designated Market Area code representing the viewers media market. Critical for local advertising sales and audience measurement alignment.

attributes.name: geographic_region
attributes.description: State, province, or region where the viewer was located during the DAI session. Enables regional ad targeting and compliance with local advertising regulations.

attributes.name: platform_type
attributes.description: Operating system or platform on which the DAI-enabled player was running. Critical for device-specific ad targeting and compatibility. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: web|ios|android|roku|fire_tv|apple_tv|samsung_tizen|lg_webos|xbox|playstation|other — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: scte35_cue_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: Society of Cable Telecommunications Engineers (SCTE) 35 Cue Type
attributes.description: Type of SCTE-35 cue message that triggered the DAI session. Indicates the nature of the ad opportunity (splice insert, time signal, segmentation descriptor). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: splice_insert|time_signal|segmentation_descriptor|provider_advertisement|distributor_advertisement|program_start|program_end|chapter_start|break_start|break_end — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: scte35_signal_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Society of Cable Telecommunications Engineers (SCTE) 35 Signal Timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the SCTE-35 cue message that triggered the DAI opportunity. Critical for synchronizing ad insertion with content breaks.
attributes.references: SCTE-35 Digital Program Insertion Cueing Message for Cable

attributes.name: session_end_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI) Session End Timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the DAI session completed. Marks the end of ad pod delivery and return to content.

attributes.name: session_start_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI) Session Start Timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the DAI session was initiated. Represents the moment the ad decision server was queried for this ad opportunity.

attributes.name: session_status
attributes.description: Final status of the DAI session. Indicates whether the session completed successfully, partially filled, failed, timed out, or was abandoned by the viewer.

attributes.name: stitching_mode
attributes.description: Method used to insert ads into the stream. Server-side stitching (SSAI) integrates ads at the CDN level; client-side stitching occurs in the player.
attributes.references: SCTE-35 Digital Program Insertion Cueing Message

attributes.name: streaming_protocol
attributes.description: Adaptive bitrate streaming protocol used for DAI delivery (HLS, MPEG-DASH, Smooth Streaming). Affects manifest manipulation and ad stitching approach.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 23009-1 MPEG-DASH, RFC 8216 HTTP Live Streaming

attributes.name: total_ad_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total duration of all ads actually delivered during this DAI session. May differ from ad_pod_duration_seconds if pod was not fully filled.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST)

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this DAI session record was last modified. Tracks changes to session status or post-session reconciliation updates.

attributes.name: viewer_ip_address
attributes.description: IP address of the viewer device at the time of the DAI session. Used for geo-targeting and fraud detection. May be considered PII under GDPR.

products.name: retransmission_consent

Captures grantor broadcaster, grantee MVPD/vMVPD, authorized markets (DMAs), consent effective date, consent expiry date, compensation terms (cash, channel carriage, promotional commitments), must-carry election status, and negotiation history flags. Governed by FCC retransmission consent regulations.

License is the regulatory anchor for consen

Removes mvpd_id BIGINT and mvpd_name ST

attributes.name: partner_id

attributes.name: negotiation_start_date

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: promotional_commitment

attributes.name: renewal_notice_days

attributes.name: renewal_option_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the agreement includes an automatic renewal option or requires renegotiation at expiry.

attributes.name: termination_clause
attributes.description: Description of conditions under which either party may terminate the retransmission consent agreement prior to expiry date.

products.name: platform_distribution_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the contractual distribution agreement between an OTT platform and an external partner (app store, device manufacturer, MVPD, aggregator, ISP). It captures platform-partner-specific commercial terms, technical SLA commitments, revenue sharing arrangements, carriage fees, launch coordination, and exclusivity windows. Each record links one OTT platform to one distribution partner with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific distribution relationship.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting operations, OTT platforms are distributed through multiple partner channels simultaneously (app stores like Apple/Google, device manufacturers like Roku/Samsung, MVPDs, ISPs, aggregators), and each distribution partner carries multiple OTT platforms. The business actively manages platform-partner distribution agreements as distinct contractual entities with partner-specific commercial terms, revenue sharing models, carriage fees, SLA commitments, launch coordination, and exclusivity windows that vary by partner relationship.

attributes.name: auto_renewal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the distribution agreement automatically renews at the end of the contract term unless either party provides notice

attributes.name: carriage_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fixed periodic fee paid to the distribution partner for carrying the platform, independent of subscriber volume. Typically monthly or annual.

attributes.name: contract_end_date

products.name: endpoint_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the service agreement between streaming endpoints and distribution partners. It captures partner-specific endpoint configurations including SLA commitments, bandwidth allocations, cost structures, and geo-restriction policies. Each record links one streaming endpoint to one partner with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific service relationship.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting CDN operations, streaming endpoints serve multiple distribution partners (MVPDs, vMVPDs, FAST operators, syndicators) simultaneously, and each partner consumes content from multiple endpoints (primary, failover, regional PoPs). The business actively manages partner-specific endpoint configurations including SLA tiers, bandwidth allocations, cost structures, and geo-restriction policies that vary by partner relationship and contractual terms.

products.name: playout
products.description: This association product represents the scheduled playout event between a delivery channel and a media asset. It captures the operational scheduling and transmission of specific media assets through specific delivery channels. Each record links one delivery channel to one media asset with playout-specific attributes including timing, sequencing, ad insertion configuration, and blackout rules that exist only in the context of this scheduled transmission.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting operations, the same media asset is scheduled for playout across multiple delivery channels (e.g., a news segment airs on the main linear channel, regional feeds, and FAST channels), and each delivery channel transmits many different media assets throughout the broadcast day. Playout scheduling is an operational business process where traffic and scheduling teams actively create, modify, and manage playout events with channel-specific timing, ad insertion rules, blackout restrictions, and sequencing. This is not an analytical correlation but a core operational entity.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the media asset being transmitted through the delivery channel

attributes.description: Actual timestamp when transmission completed, as recorded by playout automation. Used for as-run logs and billing reconciliation. Null until playout completes.

attributes.name: actual_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Actual timestamp when transmission began, as recorded by playout automation. May differ from scheduled start due to overruns, technical issues, or live event delays. Null until playout begins.

attributes.name: ad_insertion_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether dynamic ad insertion is enabled for this specific playout event. May override channel-level ad insertion settings based on content rights or programming requirements.

attributes.name: blackout_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether geographic or rights-based blackout restrictions are applied to this specific playout event. Enforces content licensing and distribution rights on a per-transmission basis.

attributes.name: playout_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of this playout event: scheduled (future), in_progress (currently transmitting), completed (successfully aired), failed (technical failure), cancelled (removed from schedule), preempted (replaced by breaking news or priority content).

attributes.description: Business reason if this playout event was preempted or cancelled (e.g., breaking news, technical failure, rights issue, schedule change). Null for completed playouts.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority classification for this playout event. Breaking news and critical content may preempt standard programming. Used by playout automation for conflict resolution.

attributes.name: sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential position of this asset within the channel's playout schedule for the broadcast day. Used for playlist ordering and EPG generation.

attributes.name: start_timestamp
attributes.description: Scheduled start timestamp for when this media asset begins transmission on this delivery channel. Used for EPG scheduling and playout automation.

products.name: channel_compliance
products.description: This association product represents the compliance relationship between delivery channels and regulatory obligations. It captures channel-specific compliance status, review schedules, exemptions, and filing deadlines for each obligation applicable to each channel. Each record links one delivery channel to one regulatory obligation with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific compliance relationship.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting operations, each delivery channel (linear, OTT, FAST) is subject to multiple regulatory obligations (closed captioning, EAS participation, children's programming quotas, political advertising disclosure, content rating requirements). Conversely, each regulatory obligation applies to multiple channels based on channel type, market, and platform. Compliance teams actively manage channel-specific compliance status, review schedules, exemptions, and filing deadlines for each channel-obligation pair as a distinct operational record.

attributes.name: effective_date

attributes.name: exemption_basis

attributes.name: expiration_date

attributes.name: reporting_frequency

domains.name: mediaasset
domains.description: Authoritative repository for all managed media files and digital objects — raw camera footage, mezzanine masters, proxy files, graphics, music beds, and archived assets. Implements MAM (Media Asset Management) via Dalet Galaxy, enforcing storage tiering, format standards (MPEG-4 ISO 14496), checksum integrity, retention policies, format migrations, and chain-of-custody audit trails for regulatory and legal hold compliance.

products.name: media_asset
products.description: Core master record for every managed digital object in the MAM (Dalet Galaxy) — raw camera footage, mezzanine masters, graphics, music beds, and archived assets. Stores canonical asset identity, technical format metadata (codec, resolution, duration, bit-rate, aspect ratio, color space, audio channels, frame rate), asset class (raw/mezzanine/proxy/archive), storage tier (hot/warm/cold/deep-archive), lifecycle status (ingest/QC/approved/archived/purged), industry identifiers (ISAN/EIDR/ISRC/UMID), originating system reference, and content classification tags. Single source of truth for all digital object identities and their technical characteristics across the enterprise.
