attributes.name: resulting_subscription_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the subscription plan that the subscriber enrolled in or upgraded to as a result of this offer redemption. Links to the subscription plan master record.

attributes.name: revenue_stream_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.revenue_stream. Business justification: Promotional offers affect revenue stream classification and promotional revenue tracking for financial reporting. Finance separates promotional revenue from standard pricing for margin analysis and re

attributes.name: sales_agent_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Sales and retention agents process promotional offer redemptions via phone/chat channels. Required for agent commission calculations, sales performance tracking, and offer redemption audit trails in s

attributes.name: subscriber_id
attributes.description: Reference to the subscriber who redeemed the promotional offer. Links to the subscriber master record.

attributes.name: subscription_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific subscription instance that was created or modified as a result of this offer redemption. Links to the subscription record.

attributes.name: applied_discount_amount
attributes.description: The monetary value of the discount applied to the subscription as a result of this redemption. Expressed in the subscription currency.

attributes.name: attribution_source
attributes.description: The marketing source or touchpoint that led to this offer redemption. Examples include email campaign, social media ad, affiliate link, or organic search. Used for marketing attribution analysis.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this offer redemption record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: discount_duration_months
attributes.description: The number of months for which the discount will be applied to the subscription. Null for one-time discounts or permanent pricing changes.

attributes.name: discount_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage discount applied when discount_type is percentage. Null for non-percentage discount types. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 25.00 for 25% off).

attributes.name: discount_type
attributes.description: The type of discount mechanism applied through this offer redemption. Determines how the discount value is calculated and applied to the subscription.

attributes.name: eligibility_failure_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the redemption was rejected or marked ineligible. Null if redemption was successful. Used for customer service and offer optimization.

attributes.name: eligibility_verified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the subscribers eligibility for the offer was verified at the time of redemption. True if eligibility checks passed, False otherwise.

attributes.name: first_time_subscriber_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this redemption resulted in a new subscriber acquisition (True) or was redeemed by an existing subscriber (False). Critical for Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Lifetime Value (LTV) analysis.

attributes.name: offer_expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the promotional offer expires and can no longer be redeemed. Used to validate redemption eligibility and track expired redemption attempts.

attributes.name: redemption_channel
attributes.description: The platform or channel through which the subscriber redeemed the offer. Enables channel effectiveness analysis for promotional campaigns.

attributes.name: redemption_code
attributes.description: The unique promotional code or voucher code entered by the subscriber at the time of redemption. Used for tracking and validation.

attributes.name: redemption_device_type
attributes.description: The type of device used by the subscriber to redeem the offer. Supports device-specific campaign optimization and user experience analysis.

attributes.name: redemption_ip_address
attributes.description: The IP address from which the redemption request originated. Used for fraud detection and geographic analysis. May be considered Personally Identifiable Information (PII) under General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

attributes.name: redemption_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the offer redemption. Tracks whether the redemption was successfully applied, expired before use, reversed due to policy violation, or rejected due to eligibility failure.

attributes.name: redemption_timestamp
attributes.description: The exact date and time when the subscriber successfully redeemed the promotional offer. Represents the business event time of redemption.

attributes.name: revenue_impact_amount
attributes.description: The estimated impact on revenue resulting from this offer redemption. Negative values represent revenue reduction due to discounts; positive values may represent incremental revenue from new subscriptions or upgrades.

attributes.name: reversal_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why the offer redemption was reversed. Common reasons include fraud detection, policy violation, subscriber request, or billing dispute. Null if not reversed.

attributes.name: reversal_timestamp

attributes.name: terms_accepted_flag

attributes.name: terms_version
attributes.description: The version identifier of the offer terms and conditions that the subscriber agreed to at redemption. Format: v1.0, v2.1, etc. Used for legal audit trails.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this offer redemption record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: zuora_subscription_number
attributes.description: The subscription identifier in the Zuora billing system that was created or modified as a result of this offer redemption. Used for billing reconciliation and revenue recognition.

products.name: subscriber_consent_record

Captures consent type (marketing email, personalization, data sharing, third-party analytics, children's data processing), communication channel preferences (email, push, SMS, in-app, postal), preferred language, consent status, consent timestamp, consent version, collection channel, and jurisdiction. Immutable audit trail — new records are inserted for each consent or preference change rather than updating existing rows. Governs both legal compliance and operational communication routing.

domains.name: audience
domains.description: Owns audience measurement, ratings intelligence, and viewership data — Nielsen ratings, GRP/TRP/HUT/PUT metrics, sweeps period data, reach and frequency reporting, demographic segmentation, and engagement metrics. Integrates with Nielsen Media Research Platform and Adobe Experience Platform to provide the authoritative audience dataset for ad sales, programming decisions, and regulatory reporting.
domains.references: Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards, MRC Audience Measurement Guidelines

products.name: nielsen_rating
products.description: Authoritative audience measurement record capturing program-level ratings data including household rating, share, HUT/PUT levels, GRP, TRP, average audience (AA), total audience (TA), cume audience, and demographic breakdowns (A18-49, A25-54, W18-49, M18-49, K2-11, etc.) for a specific program airing on a specific channel, market, and daypart. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Includes universe estimates used as denominators for percentage calculations. The SSOT for all ratings intelligence consumed by ad sales, programming, and regulatory reporting. Supports both national and local market measurement.

attributes.name: title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the program entity for which this audience measurement record was captured. Links to the program master data product.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Ericsson MediaFirst EPG

attributes.name: air_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the program episode aired on the specified channel and market. Used as the principal business event date for this measurement record.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

attributes.name: air_end_time
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the program finished airing. Combined with air_start_time to derive program duration for audience measurement calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

attributes.name: air_start_time
attributes.description: The precise date and time (including timezone offset) at which the program began airing. Used for exact scheduling alignment and daypart classification.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Ericsson MediaFirst Playout

attributes.name: audience_composition_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the program's total audience represented by the primary target demographic (typically A18-49). Indicates how well the program indexes against its target audience and is used in ad sales proposals and programming strategy.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Composition Standards

attributes.name: average_audience
attributes.description: The average number of persons or households tuned to the program during an average minute of the telecast. Expressed in thousands (000s). AA is the primary audience volume metric used in GRP and CPM calculations for ad sales.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Average Audience (AA) Metric

attributes.name: cume_audience
attributes.description: The unduplicated number of different persons or households that tuned to the program for at least one minute across all airings within a defined period. Expressed in thousands (000s). Cume measures total reach and is critical for frequency management in ad campaign planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Cumulative Audience (Cume) Metric

attributes.name: demo_a18_49_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of Adults aged 18-49 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. A18-49 is the most commercially valuable and widely traded demographic in US television advertising, serving as the primary currency for primetime ad sales.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Adults 18-49 (A18-49) Demographic Standard

attributes.name: demo_a25_54_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of Adults aged 25-54 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. A25-54 is a key secondary demographic used in news programming, cable networks, and certain advertiser categories.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Adults 25-54 (A25-54) Demographic Standard

attributes.name: demo_k2_11_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of Children aged 2-11 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. K2-11 is the primary demographic for children's programming and toy/food advertisers. Subject to COPPA compliance requirements for data handling.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Children 2-11 (K2-11) Demographic Standard; COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act)

attributes.name: demo_m18_49_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of Men aged 18-49 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. M18-49 is a primary demographic for sports, automotive, and technology advertisers.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Men 18-49 (M18-49) Demographic Standard

attributes.name: demo_w18_49_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of Women aged 18-49 in the measured universe who were tuned to this program. W18-49 is a primary demographic for lifestyle, beauty, and household product advertisers.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Women 18-49 (W18-49) Demographic Standard

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.description: The average number of times a unique person or household was exposed to the program within the measurement period. Frequency = GRP / Reach. Used with reach for ad campaign effectiveness analysis and makegoods calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Reach and Frequency Standards

attributes.name: grp
attributes.description: The sum of all ratings delivered by an advertising schedule or program, representing total audience delivery without deduplication. GRP = Reach × Frequency. A fundamental currency metric in ad sales negotiations, upfront deals, and scatter market transactions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB GRP Standard; MRC

attributes.name: household_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of all television households in the measured universe that were tuned to this program during the measurement period. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 5.2 = 5.2%). The foundational Nielsen rating metric used for ad pricing and programming evaluation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC (Media Rating Council) Minimum Standards

attributes.name: household_share
attributes.description: The percentage of households using television (HUT) that were tuned to this program. Share = (Program Audience / HUT) × 100. Measures competitive performance relative to active TV viewers at the same time.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Media Rating Research

attributes.name: hut_level
attributes.description: The percentage of all television households in the universe that had their television sets in use during the measurement period. HUT is the denominator for household share calculations and a key indicator of overall TV viewing activity.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — HUT (Homes Using Television) Standard

attributes.name: impressions
attributes.description: The total number of person-level exposures to the program, calculated as average audience multiplied by the number of airings. Expressed in absolute numbers (not thousands). Impressions are the transactional currency for digital and cross-platform ad sales.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Impression Measurement Guidelines; MRC

attributes.name: ingested_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this Nielsen rating record was ingested into the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer from the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used for data freshness monitoring, SLA tracking, and audit trail.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards; Nielsen Media Research Platform SLA

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the most recent update to this rating record in the Silver layer, reflecting revisions from Nielsen (e.g., preliminary to final, or restated ratings). Supports change tracking and downstream consumer notification.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

attributes.name: nielsen_program_code
attributes.description: Nielsen Media Research Platform's proprietary alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the program title within the Nielsen measurement system. Used as the business identifier for cross-referencing ratings data with Nielsen deliverables.

attributes.name: nielsen_report_date
attributes.description: The date on which Nielsen Media Research officially published or delivered this rating record to the broadcaster. Distinguishes the measurement air date from the data delivery date, which is critical for tracking preliminary vs. final rating release cycles.

attributes.name: nielsen_report_week
attributes.description: The ISO 8601 week identifier (e.g., 2024-W23) of the Nielsen measurement week in which this rating was reported. Nielsen measurement weeks run Monday through Sunday. Used for weekly ratings aggregation and trend analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; ISO 8601 Week Date Standard

attributes.name: put_level
attributes.description: The percentage of all persons in the measured universe who were watching television during the measurement period. PUT is the denominator for persons share calculations and complements HUT for demographic audience analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — PUT (Persons Using Television) Standard

attributes.name: rating_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of this Nielsen rating record indicating whether the data is preliminary (fast nationals), final, or has been revised. Ad sales and programming decisions must distinguish preliminary from final ratings. Preliminary ratings are typically released within 24 hours; final ratings follow within days.

attributes.name: reach
attributes.description: The unduplicated number of unique persons or households exposed to the program at least once within the measurement period. Expressed in thousands (000s). Reach is a core metric for ad campaign planning and audience delivery reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Reach and Frequency Standards

attributes.name: source_system_record_code
attributes.description: The native record identifier assigned by the Nielsen Media Research Platform for this rating record. Preserved in the Silver layer for data lineage, reconciliation, and re-ingestion traceability back to the authoritative source system.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Data Lineage Best Practices

attributes.name: sweeps_period_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rating was measured during a Nielsen Sweeps period (February, May, July, November intensive measurement periods). Sweeps ratings carry elevated importance for affiliate compensation, ad rate setting, and programming strategy.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sweeps Measurement Periods

attributes.name: time_spent_viewing_min
attributes.description: The average number of minutes that viewers in the measured audience spent watching the program. A key engagement metric used in programming decisions and content performance analysis. Expressed in minutes.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Time Spent Viewing (TSV) Metric

attributes.name: total_audience
attributes.description: The total number of persons or households that tuned to the program for at least six consecutive minutes. Expressed in thousands (000s). TA provides a broader reach measure than AA and is used for program promotion and scheduling decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Total Audience (TA) Metric

attributes.name: trp
attributes.description: Rating points delivered specifically to a defined target demographic audience (e.g., Adults 18-49). TRP = (Target Audience Impressions / Target Universe) × 100. Used by advertisers to evaluate efficiency of reaching their specific target demographic.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — TRP (Target Rating Point) Standard; IAB

attributes.name: universe_estimate_hh
attributes.description: The total estimated number of television households in the measured market or national universe used as the denominator for household rating calculations. Expressed in thousands (000s). Nielsen updates universe estimates annually based on census data.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Estimates; U.S. Census Bureau

attributes.name: universe_estimate_persons
attributes.description: The total estimated number of persons in the measured market or national universe used as the denominator for persons rating calculations. Expressed in thousands (000s). Segmented by demographic group for TRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Estimates; U.S. Census Bureau

products.name: demographic_segment
products.description: Reference master for standardized audience demographic segments used across Nielsen ratings, ad sales, and programming decisions. Defines age/gender cells (A18-49, W25-54, M18-34, K2-11, etc.), psychographic segments, income quintiles, and ethnicity classifications aligned with Nielsen and IAB standards. Used as the authoritative classification for all audience targeting and measurement reporting.
products.reference: Nielsen Demographic Cell / IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each demographic segment record in the audience measurement reference master. Primary key for the demographic_segment product. [_canonical_skip_reason: Role classified as REFERENCE_LOOKUP — this is a reference master for standardized audience demographic classification cells; per-role minimums are exempt, but MASTER_RESOURCE minimums are applied given the entity carries rich descriptive and lifecycle attributes beyond a simple code list.]
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: adobe_segment_code
attributes.description: The corresponding segment identifier in Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) for digital audience activation. Enables cross-system reconciliation between Nielsen linear audience measurement and AEP digital audience profiles for cross-platform campaign targeting and DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) on OTT/streaming platforms.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform; IAB Digital Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: age_range_max
attributes.description: Upper bound (inclusive) of the age range defining this demographic cell, expressed in years. For example, 49 for the A18-49 cell. A null value indicates an open-ended upper bound (e.g., Adults 55+). Null for non-age-based segments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: age_range_min
attributes.description: Lower bound (inclusive) of the age range defining this demographic cell, expressed in years. For example, 18 for the A18-49 cell. Null for non-age-based segments such as psychographic or income quintile segments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: cpm_index
attributes.description: Relative CPM (Cost Per Mille) pricing index for this demographic segment compared to the baseline segment (index = 100). Premium segments such as A18-49 or W25-54 carry higher indices reflecting advertiser demand. Used in Salesforce Media Cloud ad sales proposals and upfront/scatter market pricing negotiations. Confidential commercial pricing data.
attributes.references: Salesforce Media Cloud; IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Wide Orbit Billing System

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this demographic segment record was first created in the Silver Layer data product. Provides audit trail for data governance and lineage tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse environment.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity and accountability)

attributes.name: daypart_relevance
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of broadcast dayparts (e.g., 'Prime Time, Late Fringe, Daytime') for which this demographic segment has primary relevance in programming and ad sales strategy. Informs Ericsson MediaFirst scheduling decisions and Wide Orbit daypart-based ad pod targeting. Null if the segment applies across all dayparts.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; ATSC Broadcast Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic System

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: The date from which this demographic segment definition is valid and available for use in audience measurement, ad sales targeting, and programming decisions. Supports temporal versioning of segment definitions as Nielsen and IAB standards evolve.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: The date after which this demographic segment definition is no longer valid for new audience measurement or ad targeting use. Null for currently active segments with no planned expiry. Enables historical ratings data to reference the correct segment definition vintage.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: ethnicity_classification
attributes.description: Standardized ethnicity classification label for ethnicity-based demographic segments (e.g., 'Hispanic/Latino', 'African American', 'Asian American', 'Non-Hispanic White'). Populated only for ethnicity segment types. Aligned with Nielsen multicultural audience measurement standards and used in targeted content programming and ad sales. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hispanic_latino|african_american|asian_american|non_hispanic_white|native_american|multiracial|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Nielsen Multicultural Audience Measurement; U.S. Census Bureau Ethnicity Classifications; GDPR Article 9 (special category data)

attributes.name: gdpr_special_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Special Category Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether this demographic segment is based on GDPR Article 9 special category data (e.g., ethnicity, health status). When true, enhanced consent and data processing controls are required for EU audience data associated with this segment. Relevant for pan-European distribution platforms and Ofcom-regulated services.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 9; Ofcom Broadcasting Code; European Audiovisual Observatory

attributes.name: gender_qualifier
attributes.description: Gender dimension of the demographic cell. 'All' denotes combined-gender segments (e.g., Adults 18-49, Persons 2+). Aligns with Nielsen standard gender breakdowns used in GRP/TRP calculations and ad sales targeting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: The geographic level at which this demographic segment definition is applied. National segments are used for network-level ratings and upfront sales; DMA (Designated Market Area) segments apply to local market measurement; local applies to individual station markets; international for global distribution platforms.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen DMA Methodology; FCC Broadcast Licensing

attributes.name: grp_weight_factor
attributes.description: Weighting factor applied to this demographic segment when calculating Gross Rating Points (GRP) and Target Rating Points (TRP) in audience measurement reports. Reflects the relative population size and measurement panel representation of the segment. Sourced from the Nielsen Media Research Platform and used in Wide Orbit ad scheduling and campaign delivery calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen GRP/TRP Methodology

attributes.name: household_composition
attributes.description: Classification of household structure for household-based demographic segments. Used in HUT (Homes Using Television) and PUT (Persons Using Television) audience measurement reporting and in family-oriented programming and advertising targeting strategies.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: iab_audience_code
attributes.description: The IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0 standardized code corresponding to this demographic segment. Enables cross-platform audience targeting alignment between linear broadcast, OTT/AVOD/SVOD digital campaigns, and programmatic advertising systems. Used in Salesforce Media Cloud ad proposals and Adobe Experience Platform segment mapping.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0; IAB Tech Lab

attributes.name: income_quintile
attributes.description: Household income quintile ranking (1=lowest 20%, 5=highest 20%) for income-based demographic segments. Populated only for income quintile segment types. Used in premium CPM pricing tiers and upfront ad sales targeting for high-value audience packages.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: is_children_segment
attributes.description: Indicates whether this demographic segment includes individuals under 13 years of age (e.g., K2-11, K2-5). Triggers COPPA compliance controls on data collection, ad targeting restrictions, and content rating enforcement. Critical for regulatory compliance in digital and broadcast advertising.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act); FCC Children's Television Act; Nielsen Kids Audience Measurement

attributes.name: is_key_demo
attributes.description: Flags whether this segment is designated as a key demographic (key demo) for the organization's primary ad sales and programming strategy. Key demos (typically A18-49, W25-54) command premium CPM rates and are the primary currency in upfront and scatter market negotiations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Salesforce Media Cloud Ad Sales

attributes.name: is_nielsen_standard_cell
attributes.description: Indicates whether this demographic segment corresponds to an official Nielsen standard demographic cell (e.g., A18-49, W25-54). True for Nielsen-defined cells used in GRP/TRP/HUT/PUT ratings calculations; False for custom or proprietary segments defined internally or via Adobe Experience Platform.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Standard Demographic Definitions

attributes.name: measurement_methodology
attributes.description: The audience measurement methodology used to quantify this demographic segment. Panel-based measurement uses Nielsen People Meter panels; census-based uses set-top box or streaming data; hybrid combines both; modeled uses statistical projection. Determines data quality, confidence intervals, and applicability for regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC (Media Rating Council) Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: nielsen_cell_label
attributes.description: The exact Nielsen Media Research standard cell label for this demographic segment (e.g., 'A18-49', 'W25-54', 'M18-34', 'K2-11', 'P2+'). Used as the authoritative cross-reference when ingesting Nielsen ratings data and reconciling audience measurement reports from the Nielsen Media Research Platform.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Standard Demographic Definitions

attributes.name: nielsen_segment_code
attributes.description: The native segment identifier assigned by the Nielsen Media Research Platform for this demographic cell. Used for direct API integration with Nielsen ratings data feeds, ensuring accurate mapping of audience measurement data to internal segment definitions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Data Integration API

attributes.name: platform_applicability
attributes.description: Indicates the distribution platforms for which this demographic segment definition is applicable. Linear segments apply to traditional broadcast/cable measurement; digital applies to OTT/streaming (SVOD, AVOD, FAST); cross-platform spans both; all applies universally. Drives segment availability in Wide Orbit (linear) vs. Adobe Experience Platform (digital) targeting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Total Audience Measurement; IAB Digital Measurement Guidelines; MRC Cross-Media Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: psychographic_profile
attributes.description: Descriptive label for psychographic segment classification (e.g., 'Early Adopters', 'Value Seekers', 'Sports Enthusiasts', 'News Junkies'). Populated only for psychographic segment types. Derived from Adobe Experience Platform audience profiling and used in premium ad sales targeting and programming strategy.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Segment Taxonomy; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: reach_potential_pct
attributes.description: Estimated maximum reach potential expressed as a percentage of the segment universe achievable across the organization's full distribution footprint. Used in media planning to set realistic reach targets for ad campaigns and programming strategies. Sourced from Nielsen reach and frequency models.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Reach and Frequency Methodology

attributes.name: regulatory_restriction_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this demographic segment is subject to regulatory restrictions on data collection, targeting, or advertising. True for segments including minors (COPPA), sensitive demographic categories under GDPR Article 9, or segments subject to FCC advertising restrictions. Triggers compliance workflow in Adobe Experience Platform and Wide Orbit.
attributes.references: COPPA; GDPR Article 9; FCC Regulations; CCPA

attributes.name: segment_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the demographic segment, aligned with Nielsen and IAB standard cell codes (e.g., A18-49, W25-54, M18-34, K2-11, P2+). Used as the business-facing identifier in ad sales proposals, ratings reports, and audience targeting systems.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: segment_description
attributes.description: Full narrative description of the demographic segment's defining characteristics, measurement criteria, and intended use cases. Provides context for business users in ad sales, programming, and analytics teams on how to correctly apply and interpret the segment in audience measurement and targeting workflows.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: segment_name
attributes.description: Human-readable label for the demographic segment (e.g., 'Adults 18-49', 'Women 25-54', 'Men 18-34', 'Kids 2-11'). Used in reporting dashboards, ad sales presentations, and EPG audience targeting configurations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: segment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the demographic segment definition. Active segments are available for audience targeting, ad sales proposals, and ratings reporting. Deprecated segments are retained for historical continuity but no longer used in new campaigns or programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the segment by its primary defining dimension. Distinguishes age/gender cells (Nielsen standard cells such as A18-49) from psychographic profiles, income quintiles, ethnicity classifications, behavioral clusters, and household composition segments. Drives which measurement methodology and data source applies.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0; Adobe Experience Platform Segment Taxonomy

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the originating operational system of record from which this demographic segment definition was sourced. Nielsen indicates the Nielsen Media Research Platform; adobe_aep indicates Adobe Experience Platform; internal indicates proprietary segment definitions; iab indicates IAB Taxonomy-derived segments. Supports data lineage and reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Adobe Experience Platform; IAB Audience Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: sweeps_priority
attributes.description: Indicates whether this demographic segment is a priority measurement target during Nielsen sweeps periods (February, May, July, November). Priority segments receive enhanced panel measurement and are the primary basis for affiliate compensation and ad rate card negotiations during sweeps.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Sweeps Methodology

attributes.name: universe_estimate
attributes.description: Total estimated population count (universe) for this demographic segment in the measurement geography, as defined by Nielsen. Used as the denominator in ratings calculations (rating = audience / universe × 100). Updated periodically from Nielsen universe estimates and used in GRP, TRP, reach, and frequency reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Universe Estimates Methodology

attributes.name: universe_estimate_year
attributes.description: The calendar year for which the universe estimate is valid. Nielsen updates universe estimates annually; this field identifies the vintage of the estimate to ensure correct ratings calculations and year-over-year audience trend analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Universe Estimates Methodology

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this demographic segment record was most recently modified. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change data capture, and audit compliance in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity and accountability)

products.name: sweeps_period
products.description: Master record for each Nielsen sweeps measurement period (February, May, July, November) defining the official start and end dates, measurement methodology (diary vs. PPM), markets in scope, and special programming flags. Sweeps periods drive programming strategy, ad rate negotiations, and audience guarantee calculations. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform.

attributes.name: sweeps_period_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Nielsen sweeps measurement period record in the Media Broadcasting audience data product.

attributes.name: calendar_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_calendar. Business justification: Sweeps periods drive compliance calendar deadlines for ratings-based regulatory filings. FCC public file updates and license renewal exhibits tied to sweeps completion dates.

attributes.name: measurement_methodology_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.measurement_methodology. Business justification: Each sweeps period uses a specific measurement methodology (PPM, diary, or hybrid). The measurement_methodology string should be replaced with FK to measurement_methodology master for consistency and

attributes.name: regulatory_filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_filing. Business justification: Sweeps period results required in regulatory filings for performance documentation. FCC license renewals and ownership transfer applications reference sweeps ratings as public interest evidence.

attributes.name: audience_sample_size
attributes.description: Total number of Nielsen panel respondents (diary participants or PPM device carriers) included in the measurement sample for this sweeps period. Larger sample sizes yield higher statistical confidence in ratings estimates.

attributes.name: blackout_markets
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of DMA market codes where geographic broadcast blackout restrictions apply during this sweeps period. Blackout markets are excluded from certain ratings calculations and ad delivery reporting per FCC and contractual requirements.
attributes.references: FCC (Federal Communications Commission); Nielsen Media Research Platform

attributes.name: ccpa_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether CCPA viewer data privacy requirements apply to the measurement data collected during this sweeps period (e.g., for California DMA markets in scope). Governs opt-out rights and data sale restrictions for audience panel data.

attributes.name: coppa_applicable
attributes.business_glossary_term: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) Applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether COPPA restrictions apply to audience data collected during this sweeps period, specifically for children's programming dayparts or platforms. Governs collection and use of audience data for viewers under 13.

attributes.name: data_release_status
attributes.description: Indicates the current release state of Nielsen audience data for this sweeps period. 'unreleased' = data not yet available; 'preliminary' = fast affiliate estimates published; 'final' = confirmed ratings delivered; 'revised_final' = post-delivery corrections applied.

attributes.name: daypart_coverage
attributes.description: Indicates which dayparts (time segments of the broadcast day) are included in the sweeps measurement scope. 'all_dayparts' covers the full broadcast day; other values indicate restricted measurement windows. Daypart coverage affects which ad inventory can be rated and guaranteed.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; ATSC (Advanced Television Systems Committee)

attributes.name: demographic_breakdowns
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of demographic segments for which Nielsen will provide audience measurement data during this sweeps period (e.g., 'A18-49,A25-54,W18-34,M18-49,HH'). Determines which target audience guarantees can be supported for ad sales.

attributes.name: diary_return_rate_pct
attributes.description: For diary-methodology sweeps periods, the percentage of distributed Nielsen viewing diaries that were returned by respondents. A key data quality indicator; low return rates may trigger Nielsen data quality warnings or adjustments.

attributes.name: dma_list_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the Nielsen DMA market list applied during this sweeps period (e.g., 'DMA-2024-v1'). Nielsen periodically revises DMA boundaries; this field ensures correct market mapping for historical comparisons.

attributes.name: duration_days
attributes.description: Total number of calendar days in the sweeps measurement window (end_date minus start_date inclusive). Typically 28 days for standard Nielsen sweeps periods. Used in pacing and audience guarantee calculations.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: The official last day of the Nielsen sweeps measurement window as defined by Nielsen Media Research. Audience data collection and ratings calculations conclude on this date.

attributes.name: gdpr_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether GDPR audience data privacy requirements apply to the measurement data collected during this sweeps period (e.g., for EU markets included in scope). Governs data retention, consent, and anonymization obligations for audience panel data.

attributes.name: grp_guarantee_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether Gross Rating Point (GRP) audience guarantees negotiated during the upfront or scatter market apply to advertising campaigns running within this sweeps period. True = GRP guarantees in effect; False = no guarantees applicable.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau)

attributes.name: hut_measurement_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether Homes Using Television (HUT) level data is captured and reported as part of this sweeps period measurement. HUT data is used to calculate share and contextualize ratings within total available audience.

attributes.name: is_special_programming_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether special programming (e.g., season premieres, finales, major sporting events, stunting) was scheduled during this sweeps period that may inflate or distort ratings relative to non-sweeps periods. True = special programming present; False = standard schedule.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; FCC (Federal Communications Commission)

attributes.name: makegood_window_end_date
attributes.description: The last date by which makegoods (compensatory ad spots issued when audience guarantees are not met) must be aired following this sweeps period. Defined in advertiser contracts and governed by Wide Orbit traffic system scheduling.

attributes.name: market_count
attributes.description: Total number of Designated Market Areas (DMAs) included in this sweeps measurement period. Used to assess geographic coverage and local affiliate reporting obligations.

attributes.name: market_scope
attributes.description: Indicates whether this sweeps period covers national audience measurement, local market (DMA) measurement, or both. Determines which ad sales rate cards and audience guarantees apply.

attributes.name: nielsen_contract_ref
attributes.description: Reference number of the Nielsen Media Research contract or service agreement under which this sweeps period measurement is conducted. Used for billing reconciliation and SLA enforcement with Nielsen.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act)

attributes.name: nielsen_sweep_code
attributes.description: The externally-assigned Nielsen Media Research Platform identifier for this sweeps period (e.g., 'SWEEP-2024-NOV'). Used to cross-reference records with Nielsen source data and reconcile audience measurement deliverables.

attributes.name: period_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the sweeps period record. 'scheduled' = future period confirmed by Nielsen; 'active' = measurement currently in progress; 'completed' = measurement concluded and data delivered; 'cancelled' = period cancelled (rare); 'revised' = dates or scope amended post-publication.

attributes.name: ppm_compliance_rate_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Portable People Meter (PPM) Compliance Rate Percentage
attributes.description: For PPM-methodology sweeps periods, the percentage of PPM panel members who met Nielsen's minimum daily wear-time compliance threshold. Low compliance rates may affect the statistical validity of ratings data.

attributes.name: preliminary_ratings_date
attributes.description: The date on which Nielsen delivers preliminary (fast affiliate) ratings estimates for this sweeps period. Preliminary data is used for early ad sales negotiations before final ratings are confirmed.

attributes.name: put_measurement_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether Persons Using Television (PUT) level data is captured and reported as part of this sweeps period measurement. PUT data enables person-level demographic audience analysis beyond household-level HUT data.

attributes.name: ratings_delivery_date
attributes.description: The date on which Nielsen is contractually obligated to deliver final audience ratings data for this sweeps period to the broadcaster. Drives downstream ad sales billing, makegoods calculations, and audience guarantee reconciliation.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this sweeps period record was first created in the Media Broadcasting Databricks Silver layer data product. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this sweeps period record was most recently modified in the Media Broadcasting Databricks Silver layer data product. Used for change tracking, SLA monitoring, and downstream refresh orchestration.
attributes.references: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether audience measurement data from this sweeps period must be submitted to a regulatory body (e.g., FCC, Ofcom) as part of broadcast licensing compliance or public interest reporting obligations.
attributes.references: FCC (Federal Communications Commission); Ofcom (UK Office of Communications)

attributes.name: source_last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which the source system (Nielsen Media Research Platform) last updated the record for this sweeps period. Used for incremental data ingestion and change detection in the Databricks Silver layer pipeline.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this sweeps period record was sourced. Primarily 'nielsen_media_research' for official period definitions; 'adobe_experience_platform' for digital engagement overlays; 'manual' for internally-defined supplemental periods.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Adobe Experience Platform

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: The official first day of the Nielsen sweeps measurement window as defined by Nielsen Media Research. Audience data collection and ratings calculations begin on this date.

attributes.name: stunting_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of any programming stunts or special events scheduled during this sweeps period (e.g., 'Season finale of flagship drama', 'Super Bowl lead-out programming'). Populated only when is_special_programming_flag is True.

attributes.name: sweep_month
attributes.description: The calendar month in which the sweeps measurement period falls. Nielsen conducts four sweeps periods annually: February, May, July, and November. Drives programming strategy and ad rate negotiations.

attributes.name: sweep_name
attributes.description: Human-readable label for the sweeps period (e.g., 'November 2024 Sweeps', 'February 2025 Sweeps'). Used in reports, ad sales proposals, and programming strategy documents.

attributes.name: sweep_year
attributes.description: The four-digit calendar year in which the sweeps measurement period occurs (e.g., 2024). Used to uniquely identify the period in combination with sweep_month.

attributes.name: trp_guarantee_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether Target Rating Point (TRP) audience guarantees for specific demographic targets apply to advertising campaigns running within this sweeps period. True = TRP guarantees in effect; False = no TRP guarantees applicable.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB (Interactive Advertising Bureau)

attributes.name: upfront_rate_card_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether advertising rates negotiated during the upfront sales event apply to inventory sold within this sweeps period. True = upfront rate cards govern pricing; False = scatter market rates apply.

products.name: panel
products.description: Master record representing a Nielsen or proprietary audience measurement panel — a statistically representative sample of households or individuals used to project viewership to the total population. Captures panel type (Nielsen National People Meter, Nielsen Local People Meter, PPM, Diary, Return Path Data), panel size, geographic coverage (national or DMA-specific), demographic composition, panel vintage, recruitment methodology, weighting factors, and MRC accreditation status. Foundation for all projected audience estimates and the basis for measurement credibility.

attributes.name: panel_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the audience measurement panel record in the lakehouse. Primary key for the audience_panel entity.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Management

attributes.name: broadcast_license_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.broadcast_license. Business justification: Panel recruitment and weighting tied to licensed station coverage areas. Nielsen panels structured around broadcast license service contours to ensure representative sampling for ratings currency.

attributes.name: manager_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Audience panels require dedicated panel managers responsible for recruitment, retention, weighting methodology compliance, and MRC accreditation maintenance. Manager assignment critical for universe e

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.market_coverage. Business justification: Audience panels are defined for specific DMAs/markets. The dma_code and dma_name are redundant with market_coverage master data. Normalizing ensures consistency with market definitions used across nie

attributes.name: measurement_methodology_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.measurement_methodology. Business justification: Each panel uses a specific measurement methodology (PPM, diary, set-top box). The measurement_provider string should be replaced with FK to measurement_methodology for consistency. Panel-specific impl

attributes.name: primary_broadcast_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.broadcast_facility. Business justification: Audience panels are geographically recruited and must link to the primary broadcast facility serving that DMA for local market measurement, signal quality validation, and MRC accreditation audits. Rol

attributes.name: adobe_segment_code
attributes.description: Identifier linking this audience panel definition to a corresponding audience segment or profile group in Adobe Experience Platform (AEP). Enables cross-platform audience activation by mapping Nielsen panel demographics to digital audience segments for personalization and targeted ad delivery.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Audience Segmentation; IAB Digital Audience Standards

attributes.name: cooperation_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of recruited panel households or individuals who are actively and consistently providing usable measurement data. A declining cooperation rate is an early indicator of panel quality degradation and may trigger MRC review. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.8500 = 85%).
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Panel Quality Standards

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code indicating the primary country of coverage for this panel (e.g., USA, GBR, AUS). Required for international panels and regulatory reporting to Ofcom and the European Audiovisual Observatory.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; Ofcom Broadcasting Standards; European Audiovisual Observatory

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this audience panel record was first created in the lakehouse Silver layer. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for data lineage, audit trails, and compliance with SOX financial reporting controls that require traceability of audience data used in revenue recognition.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ISO 8601

attributes.name: data_collection_method
attributes.description: Technical mechanism used to collect viewing data from panel members. Electronic meters (people meters) require active button-pressing; set-top-box (STB) and smart TV ACR (Automatic Content Recognition) are passive; diary is self-reported. Determines the granularity and reliability of minute-by-minute audience data.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Data Collection Methodology; ATSC Standards; MRC Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: demographic_composition
attributes.description: Narrative or structured description of the demographic breakdowns captured by this panel (e.g., 'Age 2+, Adults 18-49, Adults 25-54, Persons 2-17, Households by income quintile'). Defines which demographic cuts are available for TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations and demographic audience guarantees in ad sales.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Reporting; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this panel was retired or superseded by a newer panel vintage. Null for currently active panels. Used to scope historical ratings queries to the correct panel vintage and to manage panel transitions during sweeps periods.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Lifecycle; MRC Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date on which this panel became the active currency measurement source for audience projections. Marks the beginning of the period for which this panel's data is used in ratings reports, ad sales guarantees, and GRP/TRP delivery calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Activation; MRC Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Breadth of geographic coverage represented by this panel. National panels project to the total US population; DMA (Designated Market Area) panels project to a specific local television market; International panels cover non-US territories.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Geographic Coverage Standards; FCC Market Definition Rules

attributes.name: measurement_currency_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this panel is designated as the official currency measurement source for audience guarantees in advertising transactions. True = this panel's data is used as the contractual basis for GRP/TRP delivery and makegood calculations in upfront and scatter market deals. False = supplemental or research-only panel.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Currency Designation; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: min_reportable_rating
attributes.description: The lowest audience rating value (expressed as a decimal fraction of the universe) that this panel can reliably report without exceeding acceptable statistical error thresholds. Ratings below this threshold are suppressed or flagged as unreliable. Typically expressed as a percentage (e.g., 0.0010 = 0.1%). Governed by MRC minimum cell size requirements.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Reporting Thresholds

attributes.name: mrc_accreditation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the MRC most recently granted or renewed accreditation for this panel. Used to track accreditation currency and schedule renewal audits. Panels must maintain continuous accreditation to support upfront and scatter market ad sales guarantees.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

attributes.name: mrc_accreditation_expiry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Media Rating Council (MRC) Accreditation Expiry Date
attributes.description: Date on which the current MRC accreditation for this panel expires and must be renewed. Expiry triggers a mandatory re-audit process. Ad sales teams must be notified of impending expiry to manage risk on guaranteed audience delivery commitments.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

attributes.name: mrc_accreditation_status
attributes.description: Current accreditation status granted by the Media Rating Council (MRC) for this panel. MRC accreditation is the industry standard for currency-grade audience measurement. Accredited panels are required for guaranteed ad buys and upfront sales commitments. Non-accredited panels cannot be used as primary currency.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: nielsen_panel_code
attributes.description: Nielsen's proprietary internal identifier for this panel as maintained in the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used for direct API integration, data feed reconciliation, and cross-referencing Nielsen ratings reports. Distinct from the internal audience_panel_id surrogate key.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Registry API

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing operational notes, known data quality issues, methodology changes, or special considerations associated with this panel (e.g., 'Sample boosted in Q3 2023 for Hispanic demographic', 'Methodology change effective Jan 2024 — includes streaming'). Used by audience analytics and ad sales teams.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Documentation

attributes.name: out_of_home_measurement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this panel captures out-of-home (OOH) viewing, such as viewing in bars, hotels, airports, and other public venues. OOH measurement is captured via Portable People Meter (PPM) technology. OOH-inclusive panels produce higher total audience estimates than in-home-only panels.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Out-of-Home Measurement Methodology; MRC OOH Standards

attributes.name: panel_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code assigned by the measurement provider (e.g., Nielsen) to uniquely identify this panel within their system. Used for cross-system reconciliation with the Nielsen Media Research Platform.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Registry

attributes.name: panel_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the audience measurement panel (e.g., 'Nielsen National People Meter 2024', 'Nielsen Local People Meter — New York DMA'). Used in reporting, dashboards, and ad sales presentations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Registry

attributes.name: panel_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the audience panel. Active panels are used for currency-grade audience projections. Suspended panels are temporarily halted due to quality or compliance issues. Retired panels are decommissioned and replaced by newer vintages.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Lifecycle Management; MRC Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: panel_type
attributes.description: Classification of the audience measurement methodology used by this panel. National People Meter (NPM) and Local People Meter (LPM) are electronic metered panels; Portable People Meter (PPM) captures out-of-home exposure; Diary is self-reported; Return Path Data (RPD) is set-top-box passback data; Hybrid combines multiple methods.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Methodology Standards; MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

attributes.name: recruitment_methodology
attributes.description: Statistical sampling approach used to recruit panel members. Probability-based sampling (address-based or random-digit-dial) is required for MRC-accredited currency panels. Opt-in panels are used for supplemental or proprietary measurement. Affects the projectability and accreditation status of the panel.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Methodology Documentation

attributes.name: refresh_frequency
attributes.description: Cadence at which panel membership is rotated or refreshed to prevent panel conditioning effects and maintain demographic representativeness. Annual and biennial refreshes are standard for people meter panels; continuous recruitment is used for large-scale return path data panels.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Rotation Policy; MRC Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: reporting_granularity
attributes.description: Finest time interval at which this panel can produce reliable audience estimates. Minute-by-minute granularity is available from electronic people meter panels and supports DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) optimization. Quarter-hour is standard for diary panels. Determines compatibility with EPG-based program-level ratings reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Reporting Specifications; SCTE Standards

attributes.name: sampling_error_pct
attributes.description: Estimated margin of error (as a percentage) for audience projections derived from this panel at a 95% confidence interval. Smaller panels have higher sampling error. Used by ad sales teams to communicate measurement uncertainty to advertisers and to set makegood thresholds for audience delivery shortfalls.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement; Nielsen Methodology Documentation

attributes.name: size_households
attributes.description: Total number of sample households actively participating in this panel at any given time. Drives the statistical reliability and margin of error of projected audience estimates. A larger panel size yields lower sampling error for low-rated programs.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sample Design; MRC Minimum Standards for Electronic Audience Measurement

attributes.name: size_individuals
attributes.description: Total number of individual persons (panelists) actively measured within this panel. Distinct from household count because multiple individuals per household are measured for demographic breakdowns used in Target Rating Point (TRP) calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sample Design; MRC Minimum Standards

attributes.name: streaming_measurement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this panel captures streaming and OTT (Over-The-Top) viewing in addition to linear broadcast. Streaming-enabled panels support cross-platform audience measurement combining linear TV, SVOD, AVOD, and FAST channel viewing for total audience reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Cross-Platform Measurement; IAB Digital Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: sweeps_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this panel is used during Nielsen Sweeps periods (February, May, July, November) for local market ratings measurement. Sweeps data drives local ad rates and program scheduling decisions. Only MRC-accredited panels with sufficient local market sample sizes are sweeps-eligible.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sweeps Methodology; FCC Local Market Rules

attributes.name: universe_estimate
attributes.description: Total projected population size (in persons or households) that this panel is designed to represent. The universe estimate is the denominator used to convert raw panel viewing counts into ratings percentages (e.g., HUT, PUT, Share). Updated periodically based on census data.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Estimates; US Census Bureau; MRC Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: universe_estimate_type
attributes.description: Specifies whether the universe_estimate represents total households, total persons, or TV households (HUT-eligible). TV households are the standard denominator for HUT (Homes Using Television) calculations in broadcast ratings.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Universe Methodology; MRC Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this audience panel record was most recently modified in the lakehouse Silver layer. Follows ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used to detect stale panel configurations and trigger downstream recalculation of audience projections dependent on this panel.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ISO 8601

attributes.name: vintage_year
attributes.description: Calendar year in which this panel sample was designed and recruited. Panels are periodically refreshed to maintain demographic representativeness as the population changes. Vintage year is used to track panel age and schedule mandatory refreshes per MRC accreditation requirements.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Refresh Cycle; MRC Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: weighting_factor
attributes.description: Numeric multiplier applied to this panel's raw viewing data to project sample observations to the total universe estimate. A weighting factor greater than 1.0 indicates the panel under-represents a demographic segment relative to the population. Used in GRP and TRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Projection Methodology; MRC Standards

attributes.name: weighting_methodology
attributes.description: Description of the statistical weighting approach applied to panel data to correct for demographic imbalances and non-response bias (e.g., 'Iterative Proportional Fitting / Raking', 'Post-stratification weighting by age/sex/race/income'). Critical for ensuring projected audience estimates are representative of the total population.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Weighting Methodology; MRC Accreditation Standards

products.name: viewership_record
products.description: Granular transactional record of audience viewing activity for a specific content airing or stream session, capturing tuning start/end timestamps, channel or platform, device type, household or individual viewer identifier (anonymized/hashed per GDPR/CCPA), duration viewed, and completion rate. Aggregated from set-top box data, ACR (Automatic Content Recognition), and streaming platform telemetry via Adobe Experience Platform integration.
products.reference: ACR Viewership Event / STB Tuning Record

attributes.name: viewership_record_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each granular viewership record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: campaign_id

attributes.description: Reference to the broadcast channel or streaming platform channel on which the content was delivered. Used for channel-level ratings aggregation, share calculations, and carriage fee reporting.
attributes.references: Ericsson MediaFirst Channel Registry; FCC Broadcast License Records

attributes.name: closed_caption_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.closed_caption_record. Business justification: Viewership sessions must track caption availability for accessibility compliance auditing. Supports FCC complaint investigation and CVAA compliance reporting by correlating viewing with caption delive

attributes.name: compliance_consent_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.consent_record. Business justification: Viewership data collection requires active consent record for GDPR/CCPA compliance. Direct regulatory link ensuring data processing legality and supporting privacy request fulfillment (access, deletio

attributes.name: compliance_content_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.content_rating. Business justification: Viewership tracking must enforce age-appropriate content delivery based on rating system for parental controls and COPPA compliance. Core requirement for subscriber protection and regulatory adherence

attributes.name: compliance_incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.incident. Business justification: Viewership data breaches or unauthorized access trigger privacy compliance incidents. GDPR/CCPA breach notification requirements mandate linking affected records to incident documentation.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Viewership data attributes content consumption to producing cost centers for ROI analysis. Content performance reports by cost center drive budget allocation and greenlight decisions for programming d

attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Quality Auditor Employee Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Viewership records undergo quality audits for billing reconciliation, ratings certification, and advertiser makegood disputes. Auditor assignment tracked for compliance trails, client dispute resoluti

The demographic_age_band and demographic_gender should be replaced with FK to demographic_segment for con

attributes.name: device_type_id
attributes.description: Hashed device identifier (e.g., hashed advertising ID, set-top box serial hash, or streaming device fingerprint) from which the viewing session originated. Pseudonymized to prevent direct device tracking per GDPR and CCPA. Used for device-level reach and frequency analysis.

attributes.name: household_id
attributes.description: Hashed/anonymized identifier representing the household unit from which the viewing event originated, derived from set-top box or ACR data. Pseudonymized per GDPR Article 25 and CCPA Section 1798.100 to prevent direct re-identification. Used for Nielsen household-level ratings aggregation and HUT (Homes Using Television) calculations.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 25; CCPA Section 1798.100; Nielsen Media Research Household Measurement Standards

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.market_coverage. Business justification: Viewership records are tracked by DMA for local market measurement. The geographic_dma_code should be replaced with FK to market_coverage for consistency with nielsen_rating and other measurement prod
