attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sales.opportunity. Business justification: Viewership data drives opportunity identification and sizing in ad sales. Sales teams analyze viewing patterns to identify high-value prospects and tailor pitches. Links actual audience behavior to sa

attributes.name: originating_broadcast_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.broadcast_facility. Business justification: Viewership records require originating facility tracking for CDN routing optimization, regional blackout enforcement, local ad insertion decisioning, and FCC local content compliance. Role prefix dist

attributes.name: privacy_request_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.privacy_request. Business justification: Privacy requests (access, deletion, portability) require viewership record identification and processing. GDPR/CCPA compliance mandates linking requests to specific data records for fulfillment within

attributes.name: production_episode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.production_episode. Business justification: Episode-level viewership tracking is standard for streaming platforms. Required for completion rate analysis, binge-watching pattern detection, and dynamic ad insertion targeting. Core operational lin

attributes.name: production_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.project. Business justification: Streaming viewership records must link to production projects for rights reporting, content performance dashboards, and recommendation algorithm training. Essential for VOD/SVOD platform operations an

attributes.name: schedule_slot_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific scheduled airing or playout event from the Electronic Program Guide (EPG) that the viewer tuned into. Links to the program schedule managed in Ericsson MediaFirst. Null for on-demand (VOD/SVOD) sessions.
attributes.references: Ericsson MediaFirst EPG; ATSC A/65 Program and System Information Protocol

attributes.name: session_id
attributes.description: External business identifier for the viewing session as assigned by the source system (Adobe Experience Platform, set-top box telemetry, or streaming platform). Used to correlate records across ingestion pipelines and deduplicate events from multiple sources.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Session Tracking; IAB Tech Lab Streaming Standards

attributes.name: subscriber_id
attributes.description: Reference to the authenticated subscriber account from Zuora subscription billing, populated for SVOD and authenticated AVOD sessions. Null for anonymous linear broadcast or unauthenticated OTT viewing.
attributes.references: Zuora Subscription Management; GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis for Processing)

attributes.name: title_id
attributes.description: Reference to the content asset being viewed, linking to the content master catalog. Enables join to content metadata including title, genre, production details, and rights windows.
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy MAM Asset Registry; EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry)

attributes.name: viewer_profile_id
attributes.description: Hashed/anonymized identifier representing an individual viewer within a household, derived from Adobe Experience Platform profile resolution or subscriber login. Pseudonymized per GDPR and CCPA. Used for PUT (Persons Using Television) and individual-level demographic analytics.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; CCPA Section 1798.140; Nielsen People Meter Standards

attributes.name: acr_source
attributes.description: The data collection methodology or source system that generated this viewership record. ACR = Automatic Content Recognition from smart TV; set_top_box = return-path data from cable/satellite STB; streaming_telemetry = OTT platform event stream via Adobe Experience Platform; panel = Nielsen People Meter panel; return_path = MVPD return-path data.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Data Collection Standards; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines; ATSC 3.0 ACR Standards

attributes.name: ad_break_count
attributes.description: Number of ad breaks (ad pods) encountered by the viewer during this viewing session. Used for DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) reconciliation, Wide Orbit affidavit verification, and advertiser delivery reporting.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic System; IAB VAST 4.x; SCTE-35 Ad Insertion Standards

attributes.name: ads_viewed_count
attributes.description: Total number of individual advertisement spots viewed (not skipped) by the viewer during this session. Used for AVOD monetization reporting, CPM impression counting, and advertiser campaign delivery verification against Wide Orbit schedules.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Ad Delivery Reporting; IAB Digital Video Ad Impression Measurement Guidelines; MRC Viewability Standards

attributes.name: audience_share
attributes.description: The percentage of HUT (Homes Using Television) or PUT (Persons Using Television) tuned to this channel/program at the time of viewing, as reported by Nielsen. Share differs from rating in that it measures the proportion of active viewers rather than the total universe. Used for competitive programming analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Share Methodology; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: blackout_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether a geographic blackout restriction was applied to this viewing session, preventing delivery of specific content in the viewer's DMA or region per rights agreements. Used for blackout compliance auditing and retransmission consent reporting.
attributes.references: FCC Blackout Rules (47 CFR Part 76); Rightsline Rights Availability Windows

attributes.name: broadcast_date
attributes.description: The calendar date (yyyy-MM-dd) of the broadcast or streaming session, in the local broadcast timezone. Used as the primary date dimension for daily ratings aggregation, sweeps period attribution, and Nielsen overnight ratings reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Ratings Date Standards; FCC Broadcast Records

attributes.name: cdn_edge_node
attributes.description: Identifier of the Akamai CDN edge node or point-of-presence (PoP) that served the streaming content for this session. Used for CDN performance analysis, SLA compliance monitoring, and geographic delivery optimization.
attributes.references: Akamai CDN Edge Network Documentation; IAB Digital Video Measurement

attributes.name: completion_rate
attributes.description: Proportion of the content asset viewed during this session, expressed as a decimal between 0.0000 and 1.0000 (e.g., 0.7500 = 75% viewed). Sourced directly from platform telemetry; not derived within this product. Used for engagement scoring, programming decisions, and advertiser reporting.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines v2.1; Nielsen Streaming Measurement

attributes.name: content_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total runtime in seconds of the full content asset or scheduled airing being viewed. Used as the denominator for completion rate calculations and to determine whether a full viewing occurred.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines; Dalet Galaxy Asset Metadata

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the viewer's geographic location at time of viewing. Used for international rights windowing compliance, GDPR/CCPA jurisdictional determination, and Ofcom/FCC regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; GDPR Article 3 (Territorial Scope); Ofcom Broadcasting Code

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this viewership record was ingested into the Silver Layer. Used for data lineage tracking, quality auditing, and source-system reconciliation.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy; GDPR Article 30 (Records of Processing Activities)

attributes.name: daypart
attributes.description: The broadcast daypart time segment during which the tune-in occurred, as defined by industry standard time blocks. Daypart is a fundamental dimension for advertising sales (CPM pricing, GRP/TRP calculations), programming strategy, and Nielsen ratings reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: early_morning|daytime|early_fringe|prime_access|primetime|late_news|late_fringe|overnight — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Definitions; IAB Daypart Standards; FCC

attributes.name: delivery_type
attributes.description: Classification of how the content was delivered to the viewer. Linear = traditional scheduled broadcast; VOD = on-demand; SVOD = subscription on-demand; AVOD = ad-supported on-demand; TVOD = transactional/pay-per-view; FAST = Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television; Simulcast = simultaneous multi-platform broadcast. Critical for rights windowing compliance and revenue attribution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear|vod|svod|avod|tvod|fast|simulcast — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines; ATSC Standards; DVB Project Standards

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Category of device used to consume the content. Used for device-level audience segmentation, ad targeting eligibility, and platform-specific reach reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: tv|set_top_box|mobile|tablet|desktop|smart_tv|streaming_stick|gaming_console|dvr — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab Device Taxonomy; Adobe Experience Platform Device Atlas

attributes.name: drm_protected
attributes.description: Indicates whether the content stream was delivered with DRM (Digital Rights Management) encryption active during this session. Used for rights compliance auditing, anti-piracy reporting to MPA, and content protection SLA verification.
attributes.references: Motion Picture Association (MPA) Content Protection Standards; ISO/IEC 23009 MPEG-DASH; Rightsline DRM Compliance

attributes.name: duration_viewed_seconds
attributes.description: Total number of seconds the viewer actively watched the content during this session, as reported by the source telemetry system. Accounts for pauses and buffering exclusions per platform telemetry rules. Used for TSR (Time Spent Reading/Viewing) calculations and completion rate derivation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Viewing Duration Standards; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: ingestion_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this viewership record was first loaded into the Databricks Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for data freshness monitoring, SLA compliance, and audit trail purposes. Distinct from tune_in_timestamp (business event time).
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy; GDPR Article 30

attributes.name: is_authenticated
attributes.description: Indicates whether the viewer was authenticated (logged in) at the time of viewing. Authenticated sessions enable individual-level audience measurement and subscriber-linked analytics. Unauthenticated sessions rely on household or device-level inference.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service; GDPR Article 6; CCPA

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this viewership record falls within a Nielsen sweeps measurement period (February, May, July, November). Sweeps data is used for setting advertising rates and programming decisions. Critical for isolating sweeps vs. non-sweeps audience behavior.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Sweeps Period Calendar

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this viewership record was last modified in the Silver Layer, for example due to late-arriving data corrections, Nielsen restatement, or session completion updates. Used for incremental processing and audit trail.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy; GDPR Article 5(1)(e) (Storage Limitation)

attributes.name: nielsen_program_rating
attributes.description: The Nielsen audience rating score associated with the program airing for this viewership record, representing the percentage of the total TV households or persons in the universe tuned to the program. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform integration. Used for GRP/TRP calculations and ad rate setting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Rating Methodology; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: platform_type
attributes.description: The distribution platform category through which the content was delivered. Used for multi-platform audience aggregation, MVPD/vMVPD carriage reporting, and OTT vs. linear audience segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: broadcast|cable|satellite|ott|mvpd|vmvpd|web|mobile|podcast|social — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FCC Platform Classification; ATSC; DVB Project; IAB

attributes.name: playback_position_seconds
attributes.description: The content offset position in seconds at which the viewer stopped watching (tune-out position within the asset). For linear broadcast, this reflects the offset from the scheduled start of the program. Used for resume-point analytics and mid-roll ad delivery attribution.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Media Analytics; IAB VAST 4.x

attributes.name: stream_quality
attributes.description: The video quality level at which the content was delivered during this session, as reported by the ABR (Adaptive Bitrate Streaming) player or CDN telemetry from Akamai. Used for quality-of-experience reporting, CDN SLA compliance, and premium content delivery analytics.
attributes.references: Akamai CDN Quality Metrics; IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST); ATSC A/322 Physical Layer

attributes.name: tune_in_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the viewer began watching the content or tuned to the channel. This is the principal business event timestamp for the viewership record. Used for daypart analysis, time-spent calculations, and sweeps period attribution.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Viewing Interval Standards; ATSC A/65

attributes.name: tune_out_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when the viewer stopped watching, changed channel, or the session ended. Used in conjunction with tune_in_timestamp to calculate duration_viewed_seconds.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Viewing Interval Standards

attributes.name: viewing_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the viewing session record. 'completed' = viewer watched to end or tune-out cleanly; 'in_progress' = session still active at ingestion time; 'abandoned' = viewer left before 10% completion; 'interrupted' = session ended due to technical failure; 'error' = telemetry data quality issue flagged.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Session State; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

products.name: reach_frequency_report
products.description: Transactional record capturing computed reach (unduplicated audience count), frequency (average exposures per unique viewer), and effective reach (viewers exposed N+ times) for a defined campaign flight, programming block, or daypart window across a specified demographic segment, market, and measurement period. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used by ad sales for post-campaign delivery validation, makegoods calculation, upfront guarantee reconciliation, and scatter market pricing justification.

attributes.name: reach_frequency_report_id

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id

Links to the demographic segment reference product sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Central to Target Rating Point (TRP) calculations and ad sales guarantees.

attributes.description: Reference to the geographic market (DMA, national, or international market) for which this reach and frequency report applies. Links to the market reference product. Used for blackout compliance, scatter market pricing, and geographic audience analysis.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Reach/frequency reports require certified analysts to validate GRP/TRP calculations, effective reach thresholds, and makegood determinations for advertiser guarantees. Analyst assignment tracked for c

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sox_control. Business justification: Reach/frequency reports support revenue recognition controls for campaign delivery verification. SOX controls test delivery documentation; links reports to control testing evidence.

attributes.name: sweeps_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.sweeps_period. Business justification: Reach/frequency reports during sweeps periods are used for guarantee verification and makegood calculations. The is_sweeps_period flag indicates relevance, but the specific sweeps period should be ref

attributes.name: audience_share_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the total viewing audience (persons using television) that was watching the specific network or program during the measurement period. Calculated as the program's audience divided by the total HUT/PUT audience. Used for competitive programming analysis and ad sales positioning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: average_frequency
attributes.description: The average number of times a unique viewer within the target demographic was exposed to the content or campaign during the measurement period. Calculated as total impressions divided by unduplicated reach. Core metric for evaluating campaign saturation and makegoods calculation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: cpm
attributes.description: The cost per one thousand audience impressions for the campaign or programming block, expressed in USD. Used by ad sales for post-campaign delivery validation, scatter market pricing justification, and makegood valuation. Confidential as it reflects negotiated commercial pricing.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Salesforce Media Cloud

attributes.name: cprp
attributes.description: The cost per one rating point delivered against the target demographic segment, expressed in USD. The primary pricing metric for linear TV advertising transactions. Used for upfront guarantee reconciliation, makegood valuation, and scatter market pricing. Confidential as it reflects negotiated commercial pricing.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this reach and frequency report record was first ingested into the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for data lineage tracking and pipeline monitoring.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Internal Data Standards; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary values in this report (CPM, CPRP). Defaults to USD for domestic US markets. Required for international market reports and multi-currency financial reconciliation under SOX compliance.

attributes.name: delivery_variance_pct
attributes.description: The percentage difference between the guaranteed audience delivery (GRP or TRP) and the actual delivered audience for the campaign flight. A negative value indicates under-delivery triggering makegood obligations; a positive value indicates over-delivery. Used for upfront guarantee reconciliation and scatter market adjustments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines; Wide Orbit

attributes.name: effective_reach_1plus
attributes.description: The count of unique persons exposed to the content or campaign at least one time (1+) during the measurement period. Equivalent to reach_persons; included as an explicit effective reach threshold field for consistency with N+ reporting framework used in post-campaign analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_reach_3plus
attributes.description: The count of unique persons exposed to the content or campaign at least three times (3+) during the measurement period. The industry-standard effective reach threshold used to assess whether sufficient frequency was achieved for advertising message recall. Critical for makegoods determination and campaign effectiveness evaluation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_reach_nplus
attributes.description: The count of unique persons exposed to the content or campaign at least N times (as defined by effective_reach_threshold) during the measurement period. Provides a configurable effective reach metric for custom campaign guarantee structures and advanced frequency analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_reach_threshold
attributes.description: The minimum number of exposures (N) used to define effective reach for this specific report. Configurable per campaign or client agreement (e.g., 3 for standard campaigns, 5 for high-frequency campaigns). Determines the N+ threshold applied in effective reach calculations beyond the standard 1+ and 3+ fields.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: grp
attributes.description: The sum of all rating points delivered by the campaign or programming block during the measurement period, representing total audience weight without deduplication. Calculated as reach percentage multiplied by average frequency. The primary currency for linear TV advertising transactions and upfront sales guarantees.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: hut_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of all television households in the market that had their television sets in use during the measurement period. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used as a contextual benchmark for evaluating audience share and competitive programming performance.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: is_makegood_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reach and frequency report has identified an audience delivery shortfall that requires a makegood (compensatory ad spot) to be issued to the advertiser. Triggers the makegood workflow in Wide Orbit and Salesforce Media Cloud when set to True.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing System; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Indicates whether the measurement period falls within a Nielsen sweeps period (an intensive ratings measurement period typically occurring in February, May, July, and November). Sweeps data carries elevated importance for programming decisions, ad rate setting, and affiliate compensation calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: measurement_period_end_date
attributes.description: The last date of the measurement window for which reach and frequency metrics are computed. Defines the end boundary of the campaign flight, programming block, or sweeps period being analyzed.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: measurement_period_start_date
attributes.description: The first date of the measurement window for which reach and frequency metrics are computed. Defines the start boundary of the campaign flight, programming block, or sweeps period being analyzed. Used in conjunction with measurement_period_end_date to bound the audience measurement interval.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: measurement_type
attributes.description: Classifies the type of measurement window for which this report was generated. 'campaign_flight' covers a defined ad campaign run; 'programming_block' covers a scheduled content block; 'daypart_window' covers a standard broadcast daypart; 'sweeps_period' covers an intensive Nielsen ratings measurement period; 'custom_window' covers an ad hoc analysis window.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: nielsen_report_code
attributes.description: The native report identifier assigned by the Nielsen Media Research Platform for this reach and frequency dataset. Used for source system traceability, data lineage, and reconciliation between the lakehouse Silver Layer and the Nielsen source system.

attributes.name: platform_type
attributes.description: The distribution platform type for which audience reach and frequency is measured. Distinguishes linear (traditional scheduled broadcast), OTT (Over-The-Top streaming), SVOD (Subscription Video On Demand), AVOD (Advertising-Supported Video On Demand), TVOD (Transactional Video On Demand), FAST (Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television), or simulcast (simultaneous multi-platform broadcast). Critical for cross-platform audience deduplication and multi-platform reach reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear|OTT|SVOD|AVOD|TVOD|FAST|simulcast — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Nielsen Media Research Platform

attributes.name: put_rating
attributes.description: The percentage of all persons in the target demographic who were watching television during the measurement period. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used alongside HUT to assess total available audience and calculate audience share for programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: reach_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the target demographic universe reached at least once during the measurement period, calculated as (reach_persons / universe_estimate) × 100. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 45.2500 = 45.25%). Used by ad sales for post-campaign delivery reporting and scatter market pricing justification.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: reach_persons
attributes.description: The unduplicated count of unique persons within the target demographic segment who were exposed to the content or campaign at least once during the measurement period. The primary reach metric sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used for post-campaign delivery validation and upfront guarantee reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_generated_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal real-world event timestamp when this reach and frequency report was generated and delivered by the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Represents the business event time, distinct from audit timestamps. Used to track Nielsen data delivery SLAs and post-campaign reporting timeliness.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this reach and frequency report, sourced from the Nielsen Media Research Platform. Used by ad sales teams to reference specific post-campaign delivery reports in client communications, makegoods negotiations, and upfront guarantee reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the reach and frequency report. 'draft' indicates in-progress computation; 'preliminary' indicates initial Nielsen delivery pending validation; 'final' indicates validated and approved for client delivery; 'revised' indicates a corrected reissue; 'superseded' indicates replaced by a newer version; 'archived' indicates retired from active use.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: report_version
attributes.description: The version number of this reach and frequency report, incremented each time a revised or corrected report is issued by Nielsen or reprocessed in the lakehouse. Version 1 represents the initial delivery; subsequent versions represent corrections or revisions. Used to ensure ad sales teams are working with the most current data.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Media Broadcasting Internal Data Standards

attributes.name: total_impressions
attributes.description: The total number of audience exposures (duplicated) to the content or campaign during the measurement period. Equals reach_persons multiplied by average_frequency. Used as the gross delivery metric for CPM-based advertising transactions and campaign pacing analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Digital Advertising Standards

attributes.name: trp
attributes.description: The sum of rating points delivered specifically against the target demographic segment during the measurement period. Analogous to GRP but scoped to the defined target audience rather than the total population. Used for targeted advertising guarantee reconciliation and CPRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: universe_estimate
attributes.description: The total estimated population size (in persons or households) of the target demographic segment in the specified market, as defined by Nielsen. Serves as the denominator for reach percentage calculations and rating point computations. Expressed as an absolute count.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this reach and frequency report record was last modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Tracks revisions, status changes, and data corrections.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Internal Data Standards; SOX Compliance

products.name: market_coverage
products.description: Master record defining a Designated Market Area (DMA) or television market — the geographic unit used for local audience measurement. Captures DMA rank, DMA code, market name, TV household universe estimate, population universe, geographic boundaries, and applicable measurement methodology (PPM vs. diary). Aligns with Nielsen DMA definitions and FCC market designations for must-carry and retransmission consent compliance.

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the market coverage record representing a Designated Market Area (DMA) or television market geographic unit.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: broadcast_license_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.broadcast_license. Business justification: Market coverage definitions derive from broadcast license service contours and DMA assignments. License technical parameters (power, antenna height) determine market boundaries for audience measuremen

attributes.name: primary_broadcast_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.broadcast_facility. Business justification: Market coverage (DMA) must link to primary licensed broadcast facility for FCC must-carry compliance, retransmission consent negotiations, local content origination requirements, and emergency alert s

attributes.name: regulatory_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_obligation. Business justification: Market coverage areas determine applicable regulatory obligations (must-carry, retransmission consent). DMA and market type drive specific FCC obligations; links market definitions to compliance requi

attributes.name: blackout_rule_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether geographic broadcast blackout rules apply to this market for sports or syndication exclusivity purposes. True if blackout restrictions can be enforced in this DMA; False otherwise. Used by rights management (Rightsline) and CDN geo-restriction (Akamai) to enforce territorial exclusivity.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76.111; Rightsline Rights Management; Sports Blackout Rules

attributes.name: broadcast_standard
attributes.description: Digital broadcast transmission standard applicable to this market. 'ATSC' (Advanced Television Systems Committee) is the US standard; 'DVB' (Digital Video Broadcasting) is the European standard; 'ISDB' is the Japanese/Brazilian standard; 'DTMB' is the Chinese standard. Determines technical playout and transmission requirements.
attributes.references: ATSC Standards; DVB Project Standards; ISO/IEC 13818

attributes.name: cable_penetration_rate
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of television households in the DMA that subscribe to cable television (MVPD or vMVPD service). Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.6234 = 62.34%). Used for carriage fee negotiations, distribution planning, and ad sales reach projections.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates; FCC Annual Video Competition Report

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code identifying the country in which this market is located (e.g., 'USA', 'GBR', 'CAN'). Required for international rights management, windowing decisions, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.

attributes.name: daylight_saving_observed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the DMA observes Daylight Saving Time (DST). True if DST is observed; False if not (e.g., markets in Arizona). Affects daypart scheduling, playout timing, and EPG accuracy in broadcast automation systems.

attributes.name: dma_code
attributes.description: Nielsen-assigned three-digit numeric code uniquely identifying the Designated Market Area (DMA). This is the externally-known business identifier used across ad sales, ratings reporting, and FCC filings. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC 47 CFR Part 76

attributes.name: dma_rank
attributes.description: Nielsen-assigned national rank of the DMA by television household universe size, where rank 1 is the largest market (New York). Used for market prioritization in ad sales, upfront negotiations, and carriage fee calculations. Updated annually by Nielsen.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The date from which this market coverage record became effective and the DMA definition was valid. Used for temporal versioning of DMA boundary and universe changes, ensuring historical ratings data is associated with the correct market definition.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: The date on which this market coverage record ceased to be effective, typically due to a DMA boundary redefinition, market merger, or discontinuation. Null for currently active market definitions. Supports slowly changing dimension (SCD) history tracking.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: fcc_market_code
attributes.description: FCC-assigned market identifier used for must-carry and retransmission consent compliance filings. Maps the Nielsen DMA to the FCC's designated market definition for broadcast licensing, spectrum regulation, and MVPD carriage obligations. Required for regulatory reporting under FCC 47 CFR Part 76.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: geographic_boundary_wkt
attributes.description: Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the DMA's geographic boundary polygon. Used for spatial analysis, blackout rule enforcement, retransmission consent territory mapping, and OTT/streaming geo-restriction via CDN (Akamai). Conforms to OGC WKT standard.
attributes.references: OGC Well-Known Text Standard; FCC 47 CFR Part 76; Nielsen DMA Boundary Definitions

attributes.name: hispanic_tv_household_pct
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of television households in the DMA that are Hispanic/Latino, as measured by Nielsen. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.2341 = 23.41%). Used for Spanish-language content distribution decisions, targeted ad sales, and TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations for Hispanic demographic segments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Hispanic TV Audience Measurement; Nielsen Universe Estimates

attributes.name: hut_base_estimate
attributes.description: Nielsen baseline estimate of the percentage of television households in the DMA that are using television during an average primetime daypart. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.5823 = 58.23%). Used as a reference benchmark for HUT-based audience projections and ad sales planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen HUT Methodology

attributes.name: market_name
attributes.description: Official human-readable name of the Designated Market Area (DMA) or television market as defined by Nielsen (e.g., 'New York', 'Los Angeles', 'Chicago'). Used in audience reports, ad sales proposals, and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: market_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the market coverage record. 'active' indicates the DMA is currently measured and used in audience reporting; 'inactive' indicates it is no longer measured; 'pending' indicates a newly defined market awaiting first measurement; 'discontinued' indicates a market that has been merged or eliminated by Nielsen.

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: Classification of the market scope. 'local' indicates a single-city DMA; 'regional' indicates a multi-city or multi-state DMA; 'national' indicates a national aggregate market; 'international' indicates a non-US market territory. Used for ad sales segmentation, carriage fee tiers, and programming distribution decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: measurement_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which Nielsen provides audience measurement data for this market. 'continuous' indicates year-round metered measurement (PPM markets); 'sweeps_only' indicates measurement only during sweeps periods (diary markets); 'quarterly' or 'annual' for smaller markets with less frequent measurement cycles.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Measurement; Nielsen PPM and Diary Methodology

attributes.name: measurement_methodology
attributes.description: Nielsen measurement methodology applied to this market. 'PPM' (Portable People Meter) is the electronic passive measurement used in large markets; 'diary' is the paper-based recall method used in smaller markets; 'hybrid' indicates a combination of both. Determines the precision and frequency of ratings data available for this market.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen PPM Methodology; Nielsen Diary Methodology

attributes.name: median_household_income
attributes.description: Median annual household income (in USD) for the DMA, sourced from U.S. Census Bureau data as incorporated into Nielsen demographic profiles. Used for audience demographic segmentation, CPM (Cost Per Mille) pricing tiers, and advertiser targeting qualification.
attributes.references: U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey; Nielsen Demographic Profiles

attributes.name: must_carry_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether FCC must-carry rules apply to broadcast stations in this market, requiring cable operators (MVPDs) to carry local broadcast signals. True if must-carry obligations exist; False otherwise. Critical for retransmission consent negotiations and MVPD carriage compliance.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76 Subpart D; Cable Television Consumer Protection and Competition Act of 1992

attributes.name: nielsen_source_market_code
attributes.description: The native market identifier as assigned and used within the Nielsen Media Research Platform source system. Used for data lineage, reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the Nielsen source system, and audit of universe estimate ingestion.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Dalet Galaxy MAM Integration

attributes.name: nielsen_station_index
attributes.description: Total number of television stations measured by Nielsen within this DMA. Indicates the competitive landscape of the local market and is used in share calculations and ad sales competitive analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Measurement; Nielsen Station Index

attributes.name: ott_penetration_rate
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of television households in the DMA that access video content via OTT (Over-The-Top) streaming services. Expressed as a decimal. Used for digital distribution planning, SVOD/AVOD audience projections, and DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) inventory estimation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Streaming Meter; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: population_universe
attributes.description: Nielsen-estimated total population (persons 2+) residing within the DMA boundary. Used as the denominator for person-based ratings metrics including PUT (Persons Using Television) and TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations. Updated annually in the Nielsen universe estimates release.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates; Nielsen Universe Estimates; U.S. Census Bureau

attributes.name: primary_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 or ISO 639-2 language code representing the predominant language spoken in the DMA (e.g., 'en' for English, 'es' for Spanish). Used for content localization decisions, Spanish-language network distribution, and audience demographic targeting.
attributes.references: ISO 639-1; ISO 639-2; Nielsen Hispanic TV Audience Measurement

attributes.name: principal_city
attributes.description: Name of the primary city or metropolitan area that anchors and names the DMA (e.g., 'New York', 'Los Angeles', 'Chicago'). Used in market identification, ad sales materials, and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA Definitions; FCC Market Designations

attributes.name: put_base_estimate
attributes.description: Nielsen baseline estimate of the percentage of persons (2+) in the DMA who are using television during an average primetime daypart. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.4612 = 46.12%). Used as a reference benchmark for PUT-based audience projections and TRP calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen PUT Methodology

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market coverage record was first created in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer. Used for audit trail, data lineage tracking, and compliance with SOX financial reporting controls that require data provenance.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this market coverage record was most recently updated in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer. Used for change detection, incremental processing, and audit trail maintenance.

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Primary broadcast regulatory authority governing this market. 'FCC' for US markets; 'Ofcom' for UK markets; 'CRTC' for Canadian markets; 'ACMA' for Australian markets; 'other' for all other jurisdictions. Determines applicable must-carry, retransmission consent, content standards, and licensing requirements.
attributes.references: FCC Broadcast Licensing; Ofcom Broadcasting Code; CRTC Broadcasting Act

attributes.name: retransmission_consent_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether retransmission consent rules apply to broadcast stations in this market, allowing broadcasters to negotiate compensation from MVPDs for carriage of their signals. True if retransmission consent is applicable; False otherwise.
attributes.references: FCC 47 CFR Part 76; Cable Television Consumer Protection and Competition Act of 1992

attributes.name: state_province_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-2 two-letter state or province code of the primary state in which the DMA's principal city is located (e.g., 'NY', 'CA', 'IL'). Used for geographic segmentation, blackout rule enforcement, and retransmission consent jurisdiction determination.

attributes.name: sweeps_participation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this market participates in Nielsen sweeps periods (intensive ratings measurement periods in February, May, July, and November). True if the market is measured during sweeps; False if it is a non-sweeps market. Affects programming scheduling strategy and ad sales pricing.
attributes.references: Nielsen Sweeps Methodology; Nielsen Local TV Measurement

attributes.name: time_zone
attributes.description: IANA time zone identifier for the primary time zone of the DMA (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'America/Los_Angeles'). Critical for daypart scheduling, playout automation in Ericsson MediaFirst, EPG (Electronic Program Guide) alignment, and ad scheduling in Wide Orbit Traffic system.
attributes.references: IANA Time Zone Database; ATSC A/65 Program and System Information Protocol

attributes.name: total_counties
attributes.description: Total number of counties or county-equivalents included within the DMA boundary. Nielsen defines DMA boundaries at the county level. Used for geographic coverage analysis, must-carry compliance, and retransmission consent territory verification.
attributes.references: Nielsen DMA County Assignment Files; FCC 47 CFR Part 76

attributes.name: tv_household_universe
attributes.description: Nielsen-estimated total number of television households within the DMA boundary. This is the principal quantitative measurement fact for the market and serves as the denominator for all local ratings calculations, GRP/TRP computations, and CPM-based ad pricing. Updated annually in the Nielsen universe estimates release.
attributes.references: Nielsen Local TV Audience Estimates; Nielsen Universe Estimates

attributes.name: universe_effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which the current Nielsen universe estimates (TV household and population) became effective for this market. Used to track the currency of universe data and ensure ratings calculations use the correct denominator for the applicable measurement period.

attributes.name: universe_estimate_year
attributes.description: The calendar year for which the Nielsen universe estimates (TV household and population figures) are valid. Nielsen releases updated universe estimates annually, typically effective in the fall. Used to version and audit the universe figures used in ratings calculations.

products.name: engagement_event
products.description: Transactional record capturing a discrete digital audience engagement action on OTT/streaming platforms — including play, pause, seek, rewind, share, like, comment, and content completion events. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform. Captures event type, content identifier, viewer session identifier (anonymized), platform, device, timestamp, and engagement depth score. Enables non-linear audience behavior analysis for programming and ad targeting.

attributes.name: engagement_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each discrete digital audience engagement action captured on OTT/streaming platforms. Primary key for this product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Experience Event Schema

attributes.name: ad_campaign_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the advertising campaign associated with this engagement event, populated when the event is triggered within or adjacent to an ad pod. Supports DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) attribution and campaign performance measurement.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit — Campaign Management; IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST)

attributes.name: advertiser_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to advertising.advertiser. Business justification: Engagement events (clicks, completions, interactions) are attributed to advertisers for performance reporting, creative effectiveness analysis, and cross-campaign optimization. Essential for digital/s

attributes.name: compliance_consent_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.consent_record. Business justification: Engagement tracking requires consent validation for data processing legality under GDPR/CCPA. Essential for demonstrating lawful basis for behavioral analytics and targeted advertising.

attributes.name: compliance_content_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.content_rating. Business justification: Engagement analytics require content rating context for COPPA compliance validation and parental control enforcement. Necessary to prevent unauthorized data collection from children viewing age-restri

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.demographic_segment. Business justification: Digital engagement events are classified by Nielsen demographic segments for audience measurement integration. The nielsen_demo_code should be replaced with FK to demographic_segment for consistency w

attributes.name: originating_broadcast_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.broadcast_facility. Business justification: Engagement events must track originating broadcast facility for streaming performance analysis, CDN edge optimization, and correlating viewer experience with infrastructure health. Critical for NOC in

attributes.name: platform_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the distribution platform (e.g., OTT app, SVOD service, AVOD channel, FAST channel) on which the engagement event occurred. Enables multi-platform distribution and audience analytics.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Environment Context; IAB Tech Lab — Content Taxonomy

attributes.name: privacy_request_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.privacy_request. Business justification: Privacy requests must locate and process engagement event data for GDPR/CCPA compliance. Links requests to behavioral data for subject access reports and deletion fulfillment.

attributes.name: production_episode_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.production_episode. Business justification: Episode-level engagement tracking identifies drop-off points, rewatch behavior, and scene-level audience response. Used for post-production feedback, marketing clip selection, and editorial pacing ana

attributes.name: production_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.project. Business justification: Engagement events (play, pause, seek, rewind) are tracked per production project for content optimization, A/B testing, and editorial feedback. Essential for streaming platform analytics and content d

attributes.name: schedule_slot_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to scheduling.schedule_slot. Business justification: Linear engagement events (tune-in, tune-out, ad interactions) must link to schedule slots for slot-level engagement analysis, ad effectiveness measurement, and audience flow tracking. Creates schedule

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.audience_segment. Business justification: Engagement events are tagged with custom audience segments for behavioral targeting and activation. The audience_segment_code should be replaced with FK to audience_segment master for consistency and

attributes.name: session_id
attributes.description: Anonymized identifier for the streaming session during which this engagement event occurred. Links all events within a single continuous viewing session for session-level analytics. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform session context.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Session Context; GDPR Article 4 (pseudonymisation)

attributes.name: title_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the content asset (programme, episode, clip, or ad) against which this engagement event was recorded. Enables content-level audience behaviour analysis for programming decisions.
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy — Asset Metadata; EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry)

attributes.name: viewer_profile_id
attributes.description: Anonymized identifier for the audience member or household profile that generated this engagement event. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform unified profile. Used for audience segmentation and ad targeting without exposing personal identity.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Unified Profile; GDPR Article 4; CCPA §1798.140

attributes.name: ad_pod_position
attributes.description: Ordinal position of the advertisement within its ad pod (group of ads in a break) at the time of the engagement event. Populated only when is_ad_event is True. Used to analyse viewer drop-off rates by pod position and optimise ad pod sequencing for revenue assurance.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST); Wide Orbit — Ad Pod Management

attributes.name: app_version
attributes.description: Version string of the OTT/streaming application that captured the engagement event (e.g., 4.2.1). Used to correlate engagement behaviour with app release cycles and identify version-specific anomalies in audience interaction patterns.

attributes.name: bitrate_kbps
attributes.description: Actual bitrate in kilobits per second of the stream being delivered at the time of the engagement event. Sourced from Akamai CDN performance telemetry. Used alongside stream_quality to assess CDN delivery performance and its impact on audience engagement.
attributes.references: Akamai CDN — Performance Metrics; ISO 23009 MPEG-DASH

attributes.name: blackout_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether a geographic broadcast restriction (blackout) was enforced for this viewer at the time of the engagement event (True) or not (False). Supports FCC blackout compliance reporting and rights management audit trails.
attributes.references: FCC — Blackout Rules; Rightsline — Rights Availabilities; Ofcom — Territory Restrictions

attributes.name: buffering_duration_ms
attributes.description: Total duration of buffering experienced by the viewer immediately preceding or during this engagement event, in milliseconds. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform quality-of-experience telemetry. Used to correlate buffering events with pause and abandonment engagement actions.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Quality of Experience; Akamai CDN — SLA Reporting

attributes.name: content_duration_ms
attributes.description: Total duration of the content asset in milliseconds at the time of the engagement event. Used in conjunction with content_position_ms to compute completion percentage and engagement depth score. Sourced from Dalet Galaxy asset metadata.
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy — Asset Metadata; Adobe Experience Platform — Media Analytics

attributes.name: content_genre
attributes.description: Primary genre classification of the content asset associated with this engagement event (e.g., Drama, News, Sports, Comedy, Documentary). Sourced from Dalet Galaxy asset metadata. Used for genre-level audience behaviour analysis and programming acquisition decisions.
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy — Content Metadata; IAB Tech Lab — Content Taxonomy 2.0

attributes.name: content_position_ms
attributes.description: Playback position within the content asset at the moment the engagement event was triggered, expressed in milliseconds from the start of the content. Core EVENT_PAYLOAD_OR_VALUE for this event log. Enables precise engagement depth analysis, completion rate calculation, and identification of drop-off points.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Media Analytics; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: content_rating
attributes.description: Motion Picture Association (MPA) or TV Parental Guidelines content rating of the asset at the time of the engagement event. Used for COPPA compliance (children's content restrictions), audience demographic validation, and parental control enforcement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: G|PG|PG-13|R|NC-17|TV-Y|TV-Y7|TV-G|TV-PG|TV-14|TV-MA — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Motion Picture Association (MPA) — Content Ratings; TV Parental Guidelines; COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act)

attributes.name: data_privacy_consent
attributes.description: Viewer's data privacy consent status at the time of the engagement event, governing permissible use of this record for analytics, personalisation, and ad targeting. Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform consent management. Mandatory for GDPR Article 6 lawful basis determination and CCPA opt-out compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 — Lawful Basis; GDPR Article 7 — Consent; CCPA §1798.120; COPPA

attributes.name: daypart
attributes.description: Broadcast daypart time segment in which the engagement event occurred, classified per industry-standard daypart definitions. Used for audience measurement reporting, ad sales daypart targeting, and programming scheduling decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: early_morning|daytime|early_fringe|prime_access|prime|late_news|late_fringe|overnight — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research — Daypart Definitions; IAB — Daypart Standards; Wide Orbit — Traffic Scheduling

attributes.name: device_os
attributes.description: Operating system of the device that generated the engagement event (e.g., iOS, Android, tvOS, Roku OS, Fire OS, Windows, macOS). Sourced from Adobe Experience Platform device context. Supports technical platform compatibility analysis and audience reach reporting.

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Category of the physical device on which the engagement event was generated. Enables device-level audience segmentation and platform distribution analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: smart_tv|mobile|tablet|desktop|set_top_box|gaming_console|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Device Context; IAB Tech Lab — Device Type Taxonomy

attributes.name: drm_scheme
attributes.description: DRM (Digital Rights Management) protection scheme active on the content stream at the time of the engagement event. Used for rights compliance verification and to ensure content is consumed within licensed windows and territories. Supports Rightsline rights enforcement reporting.
attributes.references: Rightsline — Rights and Royalties Management; Motion Picture Association (MPA) — Anti-Piracy Standards; ISO/IEC 23009

attributes.name: engagement_depth_score
attributes.description: Normalised score (0.00–100.00) representing the depth of audience engagement at the time of the event, calculated by Adobe Experience Platform based on playback position relative to content duration, interaction frequency, and event type weighting. Key metric for non-linear audience behaviour analysis and ad targeting propensity modelling.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Engagement Scoring; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Processing lifecycle status of the engagement event record in the Silver Layer. 'valid' indicates the event passed all quality checks; 'invalid' indicates a data quality failure; 'duplicate' indicates a repeated event suppressed from analytics; 'quarantined' indicates the event is held pending investigation.
attributes.references: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise UTC timestamp recording when the engagement action occurred on the viewer's device. Principal EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this event log entity. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX. Used for time-series audience behaviour analysis, daypart analytics, and sweeps period reporting.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Experience Event Schema; ISO 8601

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Categorical discriminator identifying the specific audience interaction captured: play (content start/resume), pause (playback halted), seek (position jump forward), rewind (position jump backward), share (social distribution action), like (positive sentiment signal), comment (text interaction), complete (full content consumption). Core EVENT_TYPE_OR_CHANNEL field for non-linear audience behaviour analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: play|pause|seek|rewind|share|like|comment|complete — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Media Analytics; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: geo_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the viewer's geographic location at the time of the engagement event, derived from IP geolocation. Used for territorial rights compliance (blackout enforcement, holdback windows), audience reach reporting by geography, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; FCC — Geographic Broadcast Restrictions; Ofcom — Territory Licensing; GDPR Article 3

attributes.name: geo_region_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (state, province, or region) of the viewer's location at the time of the engagement event. Used for sub-national blackout enforcement, regional audience measurement, and daypart-adjusted analytics.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-2; FCC — Blackout Rules; Nielsen Media Research — Regional Audience Measurement

attributes.name: is_ad_event
attributes.description: Indicates whether this engagement event occurred during an advertisement (True) or during editorial content (False). Critical for separating content engagement metrics from ad engagement metrics in AVOD and DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) analytics.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Serving Template (VAST); Wide Orbit — Ad Scheduling

attributes.name: is_concurrent_stream
attributes.description: Indicates whether this engagement event occurred on a stream that was running concurrently with another active stream on the same viewer account (True) or not (False). Used for concurrent stream limit enforcement per subscription terms and HUT (Homes Using Television) measurement.
attributes.references: Zuora — Subscription Entitlements; Nielsen Media Research — HUT Measurement

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Indicates whether the engagement event occurred during a Nielsen sweeps measurement period (True) or outside of it (False). Sweeps periods are intensive ratings measurement windows critical for ad sales pricing and programming strategy. Enables sweeps vs. non-sweeps audience behaviour comparison.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research — Sweeps Period Calendar; FCC — Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: isan_code
attributes.description: ISAN (International Standard Audiovisual Number) of the content asset associated with this engagement event. Provides a globally unique, persistent identifier for the audiovisual work independent of platform or distribution channel. Supports rights management, royalty calculation, and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 15706 — ISAN; Rightsline — Rights Management; EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry)

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: UTC timestamp when the engagement event was received and ingested by Adobe Experience Platform. Distinct from event_timestamp (client-side occurrence time). Used to measure event latency, detect clock skew, and support data quality auditing in the Silver Layer pipeline.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Data Ingestion; ISO 8601

attributes.name: referral_source
attributes.description: Channel or mechanism through which the viewer arrived at the content that triggered this engagement event. Used for audience acquisition attribution, marketing campaign effectiveness analysis, and content discovery optimisation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: direct|search|social|email|push_notification|in_app|external_link — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Journey Analytics; IAB — Attribution Standards

attributes.name: seek_from_position_ms
attributes.description: Playback position in milliseconds from which the viewer initiated a seek or rewind action. Populated only when event_type is 'seek' or 'rewind'. Combined with content_position_ms (seek-to position) to measure skip behaviour and identify content segments that audiences skip or revisit.

attributes.name: source_system_event_code
attributes.description: Original event identifier assigned by Adobe Experience Platform at the point of capture, before Silver Layer surrogate key assignment. Used for data lineage tracing, deduplication, and reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the Adobe Experience Platform source system.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Experience Event Schema; Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards

attributes.name: stream_quality
attributes.description: Adaptive bitrate (ABR) quality tier of the stream at the time of the engagement event, reflecting the HLS or MPEG-DASH rendition being delivered by the CDN. Used to correlate stream quality with engagement behaviour and identify quality-driven churn signals.
attributes.references: Akamai CDN — ABR Streaming; ATSC A/72; DVB — Adaptive Bitrate Standards; ISO 23009 MPEG-DASH

attributes.name: subscription_tier
attributes.description: Subscription or access tier of the viewer at the time of the engagement event, reflecting the monetisation model under which content was consumed. Sourced from Zuora subscription billing. Used to segment engagement behaviour by revenue tier for ARPU analysis and churn prediction.
attributes.references: Zuora — Subscription Plans; IAB — SVOD/AVOD/TVOD Definitions

products.name: guarantee
products.description: Master record of the audience delivery guarantee committed to an advertiser for a specific campaign or upfront deal — specifying the guaranteed GRP/TRP level, target demographic, measurement period, tolerance threshold, and makegood trigger conditions. Links to ad sales contracts and is reconciled against actual GRP delivery records. Central to revenue assurance and advertiser relationship management.

attributes.name: guarantee_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the audience delivery guarantee record. Primary key for the audience_guarantee data product in the Silver Layer lakehouse.

attributes.name: account_executive_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Audience guarantees are sold and managed by account executives who negotiate CPRPs, delivery thresholds, makegood terms, and reconciliation with advertisers. AE assignment critical for commission calc

attributes.name: advertiser_id
attributes.description: Reference to the advertiser (party) to whom the audience delivery guarantee is committed. Sourced from Salesforce Media Cloud account records.
attributes.references: Salesforce Media Cloud CRM; IAB Digital Advertising Standards

attributes.name: audit_finding_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit_finding. Business justification: Guarantee delivery shortfalls may trigger audit findings for revenue recognition or contract compliance. SOX audits examine guarantee fulfillment; links findings to specific guarantee contracts.

attributes.name: campaign_id
attributes.description: Reference to the advertising campaign for which this audience delivery guarantee is established. Links to the campaign record in Salesforce Media Cloud or Wide Orbit.
attributes.references: Salesforce Media Cloud; IAB Digital Advertising Standards

attributes.name: channel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to scheduling.channel. Business justification: Audience guarantees are often negotiated at the network/channel level for upfront deals. Direct channel link enables automated guarantee reconciliation, makegood issuance by channel, and channel-speci

attributes.name: compliance_content_rating_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.content_rating. Business justification: Guarantee fulfillment must account for content rating restrictions affecting deliverable inventory. Advertisers specify rating-appropriate placements; guarantees calculate delivery against compliant i

attributes.name: contract_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to talent.talent_contract. Business justification: Upfront sales negotiations frequently tie audience guarantees to specific talent participation (e.g., guaranteed GRPs for episodes featuring marquee talent). Sales teams negotiate rate premiums and de

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.demographic_segment. Business justification: Guarantees target specific standardized demographic segments (e.g., A18-49, W25-54). The target_demographic_code and target_demographic_description are redundant with demographic_segment reference dat

attributes.name: measurement_methodology_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.measurement_methodology. Business justification: Each guarantee specifies which measurement methodology (Nielsen PPM, diary, set-top box) is used for verification. The measurement_source string should be replaced with a FK to the authoritative measu

attributes.name: network_channel_id
attributes.description: Reference to the television network or channel on which the guaranteed audience delivery is to be achieved. Links to the network/channel master record used in scheduling and playout systems.
attributes.references: Ericsson MediaFirst Playout; Nielsen Media Research Platform

attributes.name: partner_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to partner.partner_partner. Business justification: Audience guarantees are contractual commitments made to specific partners (advertisers, agencies, networks). Tracking the partner receiving the guarantee is essential for makegood fulfillment and cont

attributes.name: political_ad_record_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.political_ad_record. Business justification: Political advertising guarantees require special tracking for equal time and reasonable access compliance. Links guarantee delivery to political ad records for FCC public file documentation.

attributes.name: production_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.project. Business justification: Upfront audience guarantees specify which production projects/series will deliver promised ratings. Required for makegood reconciliation, advertiser delivery reports, and sales contract fulfillment. C

attributes.name: revenue_stream_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.revenue_stream. Business justification: Audience guarantees define revenue recognition terms and makegood liability accounting. ASC 606 compliance requires linking performance obligations (guarantees) to revenue streams for proper recogniti

attributes.name: sales_proposal_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sales.sales_proposal. Business justification: Audience guarantees are negotiated and documented in sales proposals before being formalized in orders. Proposals specify guarantee terms (GRP/TRP thresholds, makegood provisions) that become contract

attributes.name: salesforce_opportunity_id
attributes.description: The opportunity identifier in Salesforce Media Cloud CRM linked to this audience guarantee. Enables traceability from the sales pipeline through to audience delivery commitment and reconciliation.

attributes.name: scheduling_daypart_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to scheduling.daypart. Business justification: Upfront guarantees specify daypart-level GRP/TRP commitments (e.g., Prime 18-49 rating guarantee). Direct daypart link enables automated delivery tracking, makegood triggering, and daypart-specific re

attributes.name: sox_control_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.sox_control. Business justification: Guarantee contracts require SOX controls for revenue recognition and makegood liability estimation. Links guarantee data to financial reporting controls for revenue assertions and accrual accuracy.

attributes.name: sweeps_period_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.sweeps_period. Business justification: Audience guarantees are often tied to specific Nielsen sweeps periods for measurement and makegood calculations. The is_sweeps_period flag indicates relevance, but the specific sweeps period should be

attributes.name: actual_grp_delivered
attributes.description: The actual total GRP delivered against this guarantee as measured by the designated audience measurement source (e.g., Nielsen). Populated during and after the measurement period through reconciliation with actual delivery records. Used to determine whether the guarantee was met and whether makegoods are required.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: actual_trp_delivered
attributes.description: The actual total TRP delivered against this guarantee within the target demographic, as measured by the designated audience measurement source. Populated during reconciliation. Used alongside actual_grp_delivered to assess guarantee fulfillment for demographic-specific commitments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this audience guarantee was formally approved and activated, transitioning from draft to active status. Represents the binding commitment date for revenue recognition and contractual obligation purposes.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; SAP S/4HANA Financial Reporting; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: cprp
attributes.description: The negotiated cost per rating point (CPRP) for this audience guarantee, expressed in the contract currency. CPRP is the standard pricing metric in broadcast advertising used to calculate the total value of the guarantee and to assess makegood compensation amounts.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this audience guarantee record was first created in the system. Audit trail field used for data lineage, compliance reporting, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the financial values associated with this audience guarantee (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Used in CPRP and total guarantee value calculations.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA Financial Standards

attributes.name: deal_type
attributes.description: Classification of the advertising deal under which this guarantee was established. Upfront refers to advance advertising sales events; scatter refers to last-minute ad inventory sales; direct, programmatic, and sponsorship represent other deal structures common in media broadcasting.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: delivery_shortfall_grp
attributes.description: The calculated difference between the guaranteed GRP level and the actual GRP delivered (guaranteed_grp minus actual_grp_delivered). A positive value indicates under-delivery and potential makegood obligation. Populated during reconciliation.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the audience delivery guarantee measurement period ends. Nullable for open-ended or rolling guarantees. Defines the close of the window during which GRP/TRP delivery is tracked.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the audience delivery guarantee measurement period begins. Defines the start of the window during which GRP/TRP delivery is tracked against the committed level.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: guarantee_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the audience guarantee, used in advertiser-facing documents, contracts, and reconciliation reports. Typically referenced in Wide Orbit sales orders and Salesforce Media Cloud opportunities.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: guarantee_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the audience guarantee. Draft indicates the guarantee is being negotiated; active indicates it is in-flight; at_risk indicates delivery is trending below threshold; breached indicates the guarantee was not met and makegoods are triggered; fulfilled indicates full delivery was achieved; cancelled indicates the guarantee was voided.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing

attributes.name: guaranteed_frequency
attributes.description: The minimum average number of times a member of the target audience is exposed to the campaign (frequency) committed to the advertiser. Frequency is the average exposures per viewer. Used alongside reach guarantees for campaigns with specific exposure objectives.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: guaranteed_grp
attributes.description: The total Gross Rating Point (GRP) level committed to the advertiser for delivery over the measurement period. GRP is the sum of ratings for all ad spots in the campaign, representing total audience exposure as a percentage of the target universe. This is the contractually obligated delivery level.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; GRP Industry Standard
