attributes.name: guaranteed_reach
attributes.description: The minimum number of unique audience members (reach) committed to the advertiser over the measurement period. Reach is the count of distinct individuals exposed to the campaign at least once. Complements GRP/TRP guarantees for campaigns focused on unique audience coverage.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: guaranteed_trp
attributes.description: The total Target Rating Point (TRP) level committed to the advertiser, measured specifically against the defined target demographic segment. TRP is the GRP filtered to the target audience. Used when the guarantee is demographic-specific rather than total audience.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; TRP Industry Standard

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Indicates whether the guarantee measurement period falls within a Nielsen sweeps period (intensive ratings measurement period). Sweeps periods (February, May, July, November) carry higher audience measurement scrutiny and may affect guarantee valuation and pricing.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Sweeps Measurement Standards

attributes.name: makegood_deadline_date
attributes.description: The contractual deadline by which makegood spots must be aired to compensate for any audience delivery shortfall. Critical for revenue assurance and advertiser relationship management.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: makegood_grp_issued
attributes.description: The total GRP value of makegood (compensatory ad spots) issued to the advertiser to compensate for audience delivery shortfall. Tracked for revenue assurance and advertiser relationship management. Zero if no makegoods were required.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: makegood_trigger_condition
attributes.description: Textual description of the specific conditions under which makegood (compensatory ad spots) obligations are activated. Defines the contractual rules for when and how makegoods must be provided to the advertiser when guaranteed audience delivery is not met. Sourced from the advertising contract terms.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: nielsen_order_code
attributes.description: The external order or tracking identifier assigned by the Nielsen Media Research Platform for the audience measurement order associated with this guarantee. Used to cross-reference Nielsen ratings data and reconciliation reports.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Media Research Standards

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional business context, special conditions, or operational notes related to this audience guarantee. May include negotiation history, special advertiser requirements, or reconciliation commentary.

attributes.name: platform_type
attributes.description: The distribution platform type on which the audience guarantee applies. Linear refers to traditional scheduled broadcasting; OTT (Over-The-Top) covers streaming delivery; SVOD (Subscription Video On Demand), AVOD (Advertising-Supported Video On Demand), TVOD (Transactional Video On Demand), and FAST (Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television) represent specific streaming models; simulcast covers simultaneous multi-platform broadcast. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear|OTT|SVOD|AVOD|TVOD|FAST|simulcast — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Digital Advertising Standards; ATSC Broadcast Standards; DVB Project Standards

attributes.name: rating_metric_type
attributes.description: Specifies the primary audience measurement metric on which this guarantee is based. GRP (Gross Rating Point) measures total audience exposure; TRP (Target Rating Point) measures exposure within the target demographic; HUT (Homes Using Television) and PUT (Persons Using Television) measure set usage; reach measures unique audience count; frequency measures average exposures per viewer.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: reconciliation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the reconciliation process comparing guaranteed audience delivery against actual GRP/TRP delivery records. Pending indicates reconciliation has not started; in_progress indicates active comparison; reconciled indicates agreement reached; disputed indicates advertiser has contested the delivery figures; closed indicates the reconciliation cycle is complete.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: tolerance_threshold_pct
attributes.description: The acceptable percentage shortfall below the guaranteed GRP/TRP level before a makegood obligation is triggered. For example, a value of 5.00 means delivery must be within 5% of the guaranteed level. Defined in the advertising contract and used in reconciliation against actual delivery records.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Standards; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; Media Broadcasting Industry Practice

attributes.name: total_guarantee_value
attributes.description: The total contracted monetary value of this audience guarantee, calculated as guaranteed GRP/TRP multiplied by CPRP. Represents the revenue at risk if the guarantee is not met and is central to revenue assurance and financial reconciliation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Financial Reporting; Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this audience guarantee record was last modified. Used for change tracking, incremental data processing in the lakehouse Silver Layer, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); Internal Data Architecture Standard

attributes.name: wide_orbit_order_code
attributes.description: The sales order identifier in the Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing system associated with this audience guarantee. Used for cross-system reconciliation between audience delivery records and ad scheduling/invoicing.
attributes.references: Wide Orbit Traffic and Billing System

products.name: audience_profile
products.description: Anonymized/pseudonymized master record representing a unique audience member or household identity constructed from first-party data (subscriber records, app registrations, set-top box data) and third-party enrichment (Nielsen, Adobe AEP, data clean rooms). Captures hashed identity, device graph linkage, inferred demographic attributes, content affinity scores, platform preferences, viewing recency/frequency, and consent/privacy flags per GDPR, CCPA, and COPPA. Distinct from the subscriber SSOT in the subscriber domain — this is the audience intelligence and behavioral record, not the billing or subscription identity.
products.reference: Adobe Experience Platform Profile / Audience Identity

attributes.name: audience_profile_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the audience profile record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.market_coverage. Business justification: Audience profiles are associated with specific DMAs for geographic targeting and measurement. The dma_code should be replaced with FK to market_coverage for consistency with other products. Country_co

attributes.name: nielsen_panel_id
attributes.description: Pseudonymized identifier assigned by Nielsen Media Research to link this audience profile to a Nielsen panel household or individual. Enables direct integration of Nielsen ratings, GRP/TRP, and demographic data. Null for non-panel profiles.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: ad_receptivity_score
attributes.description: Propensity score (0.00–100.00) indicating this audience member's likelihood to engage with advertising content, derived from behavioral signals in Adobe AEP and viewing pattern analysis. Used by ad sales teams for premium audience packaging and CPM pricing optimization.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Propensity Scoring; IAB Digital Advertising Standards; Salesforce Media Cloud

attributes.name: aep_profile_code
attributes.description: Unique profile identifier from Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) used to link behavioral engagement data, segment memberships, and journey analytics to this audience profile. Enables personalization and digital engagement enrichment.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Real-Time Customer Profile; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: aep_segment_membership
attributes.description: Comma-delimited list of Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) audience segment IDs to which this profile currently belongs. Segments represent behavioral, demographic, or propensity-based audience groups used for personalization, ad targeting, and journey activation.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Segment Builder; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: avg_session_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Average duration in minutes of a single viewing session for this audience member, derived from set-top box or streaming platform telemetry. Represents Time Spent Viewing (TSV) at the individual level. Used for engagement scoring and content performance analytics.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Time Spent Viewing (TSV); Adobe Experience Platform Analytics

attributes.name: ccpa_opt_out
attributes.business_glossary_term: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Opt-Out Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this California-resident audience member has exercised their CCPA right to opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information. When TRUE, this profile must be excluded from data sharing with third-party ad networks and data clean rooms.
attributes.references: CCPA Section 1798.120 (Right to Opt-Out); California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA)

attributes.name: consent_last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent change to any consent or privacy flag (GDPR consent status, CCPA opt-out, COPPA flag) for this audience profile. Critical for regulatory audit trails demonstrating timely consent management and data processing compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent); CCPA Section 1798.120; COPPA 16 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: content_affinity_genre
attributes.description: Top inferred content genre affinity for this audience member (e.g., 'news', 'sports', 'drama', 'reality', 'documentary'), derived from viewing history and behavioral signals in Adobe AEP. Used for content recommendation, programming decisions, and audience-targeted ad sales. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: news|sports|drama|comedy|reality|documentary|entertainment|kids|lifestyle|sci_fi — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Segment Builder; Nielsen Content Ratings; IAB Content Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: coppa_protected
attributes.business_glossary_term: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) Protected Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this audience profile is subject to COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) protections, meaning the inferred or declared age is under 13. When TRUE, ad targeting, data sharing, and behavioral tracking are strictly restricted per COPPA compliance requirements.
attributes.references: COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) — 15 U.S.C. §§ 6501–6506; FCC Children's Television Rules

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the audience member's country of residence. Used for rights windowing, content holdback enforcement, GDPR/CCPA jurisdictional compliance, and international distribution analytics.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; GDPR Article 3 (Territorial Scope); CCPA

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this audience profile record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse, either through initial identity resolution, panel enrollment, or first-party data ingestion. Audit trail for data lineage and GDPR data minimization compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Minimization); Internal Data Governance Audit Standard

attributes.name: data_clean_room_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this audience profile is eligible for inclusion in data clean room matching operations with advertising partners. Eligibility is determined by consent status, CCPA opt-out flag, COPPA protection status, and contractual data sharing agreements.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Data Clean Rooms Standards; GDPR Article 26 (Joint Controllers); CCPA

attributes.name: daypart_preference
attributes.description: Preferred daypart (time segment of the broadcast day) during which this audience member most frequently views content. Dayparts are standard broadcast industry time segments used for ad scheduling, upfront sales, and audience guarantee reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Daypart Definitions; Wide Orbit Traffic System; IAB Video Ad Standards

attributes.name: device_graph_code
attributes.description: Cross-device graph linkage identifier that associates this audience profile with a cluster of known devices (smart TV, mobile, desktop, STB). Sourced from identity resolution providers or Adobe AEP device graph. Enables multi-screen reach and frequency measurement.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Addressability & Identity; Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service

attributes.name: enrichment_source_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the third-party enrichment data package (e.g., Nielsen demographic file version, Adobe AEP segment refresh batch ID) used to populate inferred attributes on this profile. Enables data lineage tracing and reproducibility of audience segment definitions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Data Delivery Versioning; Adobe Experience Platform Data Governance

attributes.name: gdpr_consent_status
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Consent Status
attributes.description: Current GDPR consent status for processing this audience member's personal data for audience measurement and advertising purposes. 'granted' permits processing; 'denied' or 'withdrawn' restricts processing; 'not_applicable' for non-EU audience members. Drives data processing eligibility.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 (Lawful Basis); GDPR Article 7 (Conditions for Consent); European Audiovisual Observatory

attributes.name: household_size
attributes.description: Estimated number of persons in the audience household, derived from Nielsen panel data or set-top box signals. Used in HUT (Homes Using Television) and PUT (Persons Using Television) calculations for audience measurement reporting.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — HUT/PUT Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement

attributes.name: hut_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this household-level audience profile is eligible to be counted in HUT (Homes Using Television) calculations. HUT measures the percentage of TV-equipped homes actively watching television during a given time period, a foundational metric for broadcast ratings.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — HUT Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: identity_confidence_score
attributes.description: Confidence score (0.00–100.00) representing the reliability of the identity resolution that constructed this audience profile. Higher scores indicate stronger deterministic matching (e.g., authenticated login); lower scores indicate probabilistic device-graph inference. Used to qualify profiles for premium ad targeting.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Addressability & Identity Framework; Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service

attributes.name: identity_hash
attributes.description: SHA-256 pseudonymized hash of the audience member's primary identity (e.g., email or subscriber ID) used for cross-platform identity resolution without exposing raw PII. Enables privacy-safe linkage across Nielsen, Adobe AEP, and first-party data sources.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4 & Article 25 (Privacy by Design); CCPA Section 1798.140

attributes.name: identity_source
attributes.description: Originating source of the audience identity construction: 'first_party' (subscriber or app registration data), 'nielsen' (Nielsen Media Research panel linkage), 'adobe_aep' (Adobe Experience Platform profile), 'set_top_box' (STB device-level data), 'clean_room' (data clean room match), or 'modeled' (probabilistic inference).
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Adobe Experience Platform; IAB Data Transparency Standards

attributes.name: income_band
attributes.description: Inferred household income band derived from third-party demographic enrichment (Nielsen, data clean rooms). Used for premium audience segmentation in upfront and scatter market ad sales, enabling CPM pricing differentiation by audience affluence.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Enrichment; IAB Audience Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: inferred_age_band
attributes.description: Inferred age demographic band for the audience member, derived from Nielsen panel data, set-top box signals, or modeled enrichment. Used for GRP/TRP demographic targeting and ad sales audience guarantees. Not directly collected from the individual.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Segmentation; IAB Audience Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: inferred_gender
attributes.description: Inferred gender of the audience member derived from panel data or modeled signals. Used for demographic audience targeting in ad sales (GRP/TRP calculations) and programming decisions. Not directly collected.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Segmentation; IAB Audience Taxonomy v3

attributes.name: last_seen_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent observed audience activity event (viewing session, app interaction, or platform login) for this profile. Used to determine audience recency, drive re-engagement campaigns, and calculate viewing recency metrics.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Profile Last Activity; Nielsen Audience Engagement

attributes.name: nielsen_grp_index
attributes.description: Indexed GRP (Gross Rating Point) score for this audience profile relative to the total population, sourced from Nielsen Media Research. A GRP index above 100 indicates above-average exposure to rated content. Used in ad sales audience guarantees and upfront negotiations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — GRP Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: panel_weight_factor
attributes.description: Statistical weighting factor assigned by Nielsen to this panel member profile to project panel observations to the total population. Applied in GRP, TRP, HUT, and PUT calculations. Null for non-panel (modeled or first-party only) profiles.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Panel Weighting Methodology; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: platform_preference
attributes.description: Primary viewing platform preference inferred from behavioral signals: 'linear_tv' (traditional scheduled broadcast), 'svod' (Subscription Video On Demand), 'avod' (Advertising-Supported VOD), 'tvod' (Transactional VOD), 'fast' (Free Ad-Supported Streaming TV), 'ott' (Over-The-Top), 'mvpd' (Multichannel Video Programming Distributor), or 'vmvpd' (Virtual MVPD). Drives distribution strategy and ad product targeting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear_tv|svod|avod|tvod|fast|ott|mvpd|vmvpd — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Ad Spend Report; ATSC 3.0 Standards; DVB Project

attributes.name: primary_device_type
attributes.description: The primary device type through which this audience member most frequently consumes content, derived from device graph and behavioral data. Used for CDN delivery optimization, ad format targeting, and platform analytics.
attributes.references: IAB Tech Lab — Device Type Taxonomy; Akamai CDN Analytics

attributes.name: profile_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the audience profile. 'suppressed' indicates a privacy opt-out or regulatory hold; 'pending_consent' indicates consent collection is in progress; 'purged' indicates the record has been anonymized per GDPR/CCPA erasure request.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure); CCPA Section 1798.105; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: profile_type
attributes.description: Classification of the audience profile record: 'individual' (single person identity), 'household' (aggregated household unit), 'panel_member' (Nielsen or equivalent panel participant), or 'modeled' (synthetically constructed from behavioral signals without direct identity linkage).
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Audience Segmentation Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: sweeps_period_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this audience profile's measurement data was captured during a Nielsen Sweeps period (intensive ratings measurement period: February, May, July, November). Sweeps data carries higher statistical weight in ratings calculations and programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sweeps Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: trp_index
attributes.description: Indexed TRP (Target Rating Point) score representing this audience member's contribution to a specific demographic target group's rating. Distinct from GRP in that it measures reach within a defined target demographic. Used for demographic-specific ad campaign planning and post-campaign analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — TRP Methodology; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this audience profile record, triggered by enrichment refresh, consent status change, identity graph update, or behavioral signal ingestion. Used for data freshness monitoring and incremental processing.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Accuracy); Internal Data Governance Audit Standard; Adobe Experience Platform

attributes.name: viewing_recency_days
attributes.description: Number of days since this audience member last engaged with any content on any tracked platform. Used for audience recency segmentation, churn prediction, and re-engagement campaign targeting. Lower values indicate more recently active audiences.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform — Recency-Frequency-Monetary (RFM) Segmentation; Nielsen Audience Engagement Metrics

attributes.name: weekly_viewing_frequency
attributes.description: Average number of distinct viewing sessions per week for this audience member, calculated over a rolling 4-week window. Represents the Frequency dimension of audience measurement (average exposures per viewer). Used in reach and frequency reporting for ad campaign delivery.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Reach and Frequency Methodology; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

products.name: measurement_methodology
products.description: Reference master defining the audience measurement methodologies in use — Nielsen PPM (Portable People Meter), Nielsen Diary, Set-Top Box (STB) data, ACR (Automatic Content Recognition), streaming platform telemetry, and hybrid cross-platform measurement. Captures methodology code, description, applicable market types, sample size requirements, reporting latency, and accreditation body (MRC — Media Rating Council). Governs how each viewership and rating record is interpreted.

attributes.name: measurement_methodology_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each audience measurement methodology record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this reference master entity. [_canonical_skip_reason: REFERENCE_LOOKUP — this entity is a reference master defining enumerated measurement methodologies; per-role minimums are exempt, but comprehensive coverage is still applied given the business complexity of this domain.]
attributes.references: Media Rating Council (MRC) Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: accreditation_body
attributes.description: The name of the independent body that has accredited or audited this measurement methodology (e.g., 'Media Rating Council (MRC)', 'Joint Industry Committee (JIC)', 'BARB', 'Ofcom'). Supports multi-market operations where different accreditation bodies govern different geographies.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards; Ofcom Broadcasting Standards; European Audiovisual Observatory

attributes.name: applicable_market_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of market types where this methodology is valid (e.g., 'national, local_dma, regional, international'). Nielsen PPM is typically used in national and large local DMA markets; diary methodology is used in smaller local markets. Determines which geographic market audience records can be attributed to this methodology.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Market Coverage Documentation; FCC Broadcast Licensing

attributes.name: applicable_platform_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of platform types to which this methodology applies (e.g., 'linear_tv, ott_streaming, radio, digital_display, podcast'). Governs which viewership records and distribution channels can be measured and reported using this methodology. Critical for cross-platform audience deduplication and hybrid measurement.
attributes.references: IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines; MRC Cross-Platform Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: audience_metric_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of audience metrics that this methodology can produce (e.g., 'GRP, TRP, HUT, PUT, reach, frequency, share, Nielsen_rating, TSR, CPRP'). Governs which KPIs can be reported using data collected under this methodology. GRP (Gross Rating Point), TRP (Target Rating Point), HUT (Homes Using Television), PUT (Persons Using Television), TSR (Time Spent Reading/Viewing), CPRP (Cost Per Rating Point).
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines; MRC Minimum Standards

attributes.name: consent_mechanism_required
attributes.description: The type of audience consent mechanism required for data collection under this methodology: opt_in (explicit consent required before data collection), opt_out (data collected unless individual opts out), panel_agreement (panelists sign participation agreement), no_consent_required (census/aggregate data with no individual tracking), or mixed. Governs GDPR, CCPA, and COPPA compliance posture.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6 and 7; CCPA Section 1798.120; COPPA 16 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this measurement methodology record was first created in the Silver Layer data product. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and change management tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: cross_platform_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this methodology supports cross-platform audience deduplication and unified reach/frequency reporting across linear TV, OTT (Over-The-Top), digital, and streaming platforms. Cross-platform capability is required for total audience measurement (TAM) reporting and advanced advertising guarantees.
attributes.references: MRC Cross-Platform Audience Measurement Standards; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: currency_standard
attributes.description: The audience measurement currency standard supported by this methodology, defining the viewing window used for commercial ratings: C3 (average commercial ratings including 3 days of DVR playback), C7 (7-day DVR playback), C35 (35-day), live_plus_same_day, live_only, or custom. The currency standard is the contractual basis for ad sales guarantees and makegood calculations in upfront and scatter markets.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Currency Standards; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: data_collection_mechanism
attributes.description: The specific technical mechanism by which audience exposure data is collected: PPM device (Portable People Meter worn by panelists), diary form (paper or electronic self-report), STB return path (Set-Top Box return-path data), ACR fingerprint (Automatic Content Recognition audio/video fingerprinting), SDK telemetry (streaming app software development kit), pixel tracking (web/app pixel), or hybrid combination. Determines data fidelity and applicable use cases. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ppm_device|diary_form|stb_return_path|acr_fingerprint|sdk_telemetry|pixel_tracking|hybrid — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ATSC Standards; DVB Project Technical Standards; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: data_retention_days
attributes.description: The maximum number of days that raw audience measurement data collected under this methodology may be retained, as governed by privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) and MRC audit requirements. After this period, data must be anonymized or deleted. Drives data lifecycle management in the lakehouse.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5(1)(e); CCPA Section 1798.100; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: daypart_applicability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of broadcast dayparts for which this methodology produces valid audience estimates (e.g., 'early_morning, daytime, early_fringe, prime_time, late_news, overnight'). Daypart is a standard time segment of the broadcast day used in ad scheduling and CPM pricing. Some methodologies may have reduced reliability in overnight or early morning dayparts.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Daypart Definitions; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: deduplication_method
attributes.description: The method used to deduplicate audience reach across platforms or devices when this methodology is applied in cross-platform measurement: probabilistic (statistical modeling), deterministic (identity-matched), hybrid (combination), or none (single-platform only). Affects reported unique reach figures and frequency calculations.
attributes.references: MRC Cross-Platform Audience Measurement Standards; IAB Identity Resolution Framework

attributes.name: demographic_granularity
attributes.description: Describes the level of demographic segmentation this methodology supports (e.g., 'age_sex_only', 'age_sex_income', 'full_psychographic', 'household_level_only'). Determines which audience segments can be reported for ad targeting, TRP calculations, and upfront sales guarantees.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Demographic Reporting; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The date from which this measurement methodology became or becomes valid for use in audience measurement, ratings reporting, and ad sales guarantees. Supports temporal validity tracking for methodology versioning and historical ratings restatement.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Media Research Platform

attributes.name: effective_until_date
attributes.description: The date on which this measurement methodology ceases to be valid for new audience measurement records. Null indicates the methodology is currently open-ended and active. Used to enforce temporal validity in ratings lookups and prevent application of deprecated methodologies to new viewership data.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Media Research Platform

attributes.name: geographic_coverage_level
attributes.description: The geographic scope at which this methodology provides valid audience measurement: national (US-wide), dma (Designated Market Area), regional, local (sub-DMA), international, or global. Determines applicability for local vs. national ad sales, retransmission consent negotiations, and blackout enforcement.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Market Coverage; FCC Broadcast Licensing; Ofcom

attributes.name: is_sweeps_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this measurement methodology is used or enhanced during Nielsen Sweeps periods (February, May, July, November) — the intensive ratings measurement periods used to set local advertising rates. Diary methodology is exclusively sweeps-based in many markets; PPM operates year-round.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Sweeps Methodology; FCC Sweeps Period Regulations

attributes.name: methodology_code
attributes.description: Short, externally-recognized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the measurement methodology (e.g., NIELSEN_PPM, NIELSEN_DIARY, STB_DATA, ACR, STREAMING_TELEMETRY, HYBRID_XPLATFORM). Used as a stable business key across systems including Nielsen Media Research Platform and Adobe Experience Platform integrations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Methodology Registry; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: methodology_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of how the measurement methodology works, including data collection mechanism, panel recruitment approach, weighting procedures, and any known limitations. Used by ad sales teams, programming analysts, and regulatory compliance officers to understand how viewership and rating records are produced.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Media Research Platform Documentation

attributes.name: methodology_name
attributes.description: Full human-readable name of the audience measurement methodology (e.g., 'Nielsen Portable People Meter', 'Nielsen Diary', 'Set-Top Box Data', 'Automatic Content Recognition', 'Streaming Platform Telemetry', 'Hybrid Cross-Platform Measurement'). Used in reports, dashboards, and regulatory filings.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: methodology_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the measurement methodology within the organization's audience measurement framework. Active methodologies are used in current ratings and GRP/TRP reporting; deprecated or retired methodologies are retained for historical record interpretation; pilot methodologies are under evaluation for MRC accreditation.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement

attributes.name: methodology_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the measurement approach: passive (device-based passive capture such as PPM or STB), diary (self-reported viewer logs), census (full population streaming telemetry), hybrid (cross-platform combination), panel (statistically sampled panel), or acr (Automatic Content Recognition fingerprinting). Governs how ratings and GRP/TRP calculations are interpreted.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: mrc_accreditation_code
attributes.description: The official accreditation reference number issued by the Media Rating Council (MRC) for this measurement methodology. Used in regulatory filings, ad sales contracts, and audit documentation to reference the specific MRC accreditation certificate.

attributes.name: mrc_accreditation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the Media Rating Council (MRC) granted or last renewed accreditation for this measurement methodology. Used to track accreditation currency and trigger renewal workflows.

attributes.name: mrc_accreditation_expiry_date
attributes.business_glossary_term: Media Rating Council (MRC) Accreditation Expiry Date
attributes.description: The date on which the current MRC accreditation for this methodology expires. Methodologies with lapsed accreditation cannot be used in contractually binding audience guarantees for upfront or scatter market ad sales. Triggers compliance review and renewal workflows.

attributes.name: mrc_accreditation_status
attributes.description: Current accreditation status granted by the Media Rating Council (MRC) for this measurement methodology. MRC accreditation is the industry standard for validating audience measurement quality and is required for use in upfront and scatter market ad sales negotiations. Accredited methodologies carry full contractual weight; conditionally accredited methodologies may have usage restrictions.
attributes.references: Media Rating Council (MRC) Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, known limitations, special handling instructions, or contextual information about this measurement methodology. Examples include known panel biases, market-specific adjustments, or transition notes when migrating from one methodology version to another.
attributes.references: Internal Data Governance Policy; MRC Audit Documentation Standards

attributes.name: privacy_compliance_framework
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of privacy and data protection frameworks under which this methodology's data collection and processing is compliant (e.g., 'GDPR, CCPA, COPPA, TCPA'). GDPR governs EU audience data; CCPA governs California viewer data; COPPA governs children's content measurement. Required for regulatory reporting and data governance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5; CCPA Section 1798; COPPA 16 CFR Part 312; FCC Privacy Rules

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: The cadence at which audience measurement data is reported using this methodology: overnight (daily ratings delivery), weekly, monthly, quarterly, or sweeps_only (data available only during Nielsen Sweeps measurement periods in February, May, July, and November). Governs scheduling of ad sales reporting and programming analysis cycles.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; FCC Sweeps Period Regulations

attributes.name: reporting_latency_hours
attributes.description: The typical number of hours between the audience exposure event and the availability of processed, reportable ratings data using this methodology. Nielsen PPM typically delivers overnight ratings within 24 hours; diary methodology may have 2–4 week latency. Critical for ad sales makegoods, scatter market decisions, and programming adjustments.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Delivery SLA Documentation; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: sample_size_minimum
attributes.description: The minimum number of panelists or measurement units required for this methodology to produce statistically valid audience estimates. Below this threshold, ratings data is considered unreliable and may be suppressed or flagged. Enforced per MRC accreditation requirements and Nielsen panel design standards.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Panel Design Specifications

attributes.name: sample_size_target
attributes.description: The ideal or design target number of panelists or measurement units for this methodology to achieve the desired statistical confidence level and margin of error. Used in panel management and methodology performance monitoring against MRC accreditation benchmarks.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Standards for Audience Measurement; Nielsen Panel Design Specifications

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this methodology definition originates (e.g., 'NIELSEN_MRP' for Nielsen Media Research Platform, 'ADOBE_AEP' for Adobe Experience Platform). Used for data lineage tracking and Silver Layer ingestion audit in the Databricks Lakehouse.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Adobe Experience Platform; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this measurement methodology record was most recently modified in the Silver Layer data product. Used for incremental load detection, change data capture, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: vendor_methodology_version
attributes.description: The vendor-assigned version identifier for this measurement methodology (e.g., 'PPM v3.2', 'C3', 'C7', 'P2+ 2023'). Version changes may affect historical comparability of ratings data and require restatement of audience guarantees. Critical for audit trails and makegood calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform — Methodology Versioning; MRC Audit Standards

attributes.name: vendor_name
attributes.description: The name of the third-party vendor or research firm that operates or provides this measurement methodology (e.g., 'Nielsen', 'Comscore', 'Kantar', 'VideoAmp', 'iSpot.tv'). Used for vendor management, contract tracking, and source system attribution in the Nielsen Media Research Platform integration.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

products.name: segment
products.description: Master record for a defined, reusable audience segment built from demographic, behavioral, and psychographic criteria for use in ad targeting, programming strategy, and content personalization. Captures segment name, definition logic, estimated size, demographic composition, platform applicability, activation status, and data source (Nielsen, Adobe AEP, first-party). Distinct from demographic_segment (which is a reference classification) — this is an operationally managed, business-owned targeting segment.
products.reference: Adobe AEP Segment / Nielsen Audience Segment

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the audience segment record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this master resource entity.

attributes.name: coppa_declaration_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.coppa_declaration. Business justification: Audience segments targeting children must link to COPPA compliance declarations. Ensures parental consent mechanisms are in place before segment activation for advertising or analytics.

attributes.name: activation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the segment governing whether it is available for use in ad targeting, campaign activation, or content personalization. 'draft' indicates under construction; 'pending_review' awaits compliance or data governance approval; 'active' is live and deployable; 'inactive' is suspended; 'archived' is retired.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Segment Lifecycle; IAB Data Transparency Standards

attributes.name: aep_segment_code
attributes.description: The segment identifier as defined and managed within Adobe Experience Platform (AEP). Used for digital audience activation, personalization journeys, and cross-channel targeting. Enables synchronization between the internal audience_segment master record and the AEP segment definition for OTT and digital platforms.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Segment Builder API; IAB Data Transparency Standards

attributes.name: age_range_max
attributes.description: Maximum age (inclusive) of the primary demographic target for this segment, expressed in years. Used with age_range_min to define the Nielsen demographic cell. A null value indicates an open-ended upper bound (e.g., '55+' segments).
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Demographic Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: age_range_min
attributes.description: Minimum age (inclusive) of the primary demographic target for this segment, expressed in years. Used in conjunction with age_range_max to define the Nielsen demographic cell (e.g., 25 for the 'Adults 25-54' standard Nielsen demo). Null if the segment is not age-bounded.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Demographic Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the data governance or compliance approver who authorized this segment for activation, particularly for segments involving sensitive demographic data, COPPA-restricted audiences, or GDPR-regulated EU audiences. Supports audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Accountability Principle); COPPA Compliance; Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this segment received formal data governance or compliance approval for activation. Distinct from created_timestamp — captures the approval lifecycle event. Required for GDPR accountability documentation and internal audit trails. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Accountability Principle); Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: content_genre_affinity
attributes.description: Primary content genre(s) this segment shows strong viewership affinity toward, used for programming strategy alignment and contextual ad targeting (e.g., 'drama,sports,news'). Sourced from Nielsen viewing behavior data or Adobe AEP content interaction signals. Informs content acquisition decisions and ad pod placement strategy.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Content Affinity Reports; IAB Content Taxonomy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this audience segment record was first created in the system. Serves as the audit creation timestamp for data lineage, governance, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Confidentiality); SOX Section 404 (Internal Controls); Media Broadcasting Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the primary data origin used to construct the segment. 'nielsen' indicates Nielsen Media Research Platform ratings and demographic data; 'adobe_aep' indicates Adobe Experience Platform behavioral profiles; 'first_party' indicates proprietary subscriber or registration data; 'third_party' indicates licensed external data; 'hybrid' indicates a combination of multiple sources.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Adobe Experience Platform; IAB Data Transparency Standards

attributes.name: daypart_applicability
attributes.description: Broadcast daypart(s) for which this segment is most relevant or has been validated, expressed as a comma-delimited list of standard daypart labels (e.g., 'primetime,late_night'). Daypart is a standard media-buying time segment of the broadcast day used in ad scheduling and upfront sales. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: early_morning|daytime|early_fringe|primetime|late_news|late_night|overnight — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Daypart Definitions; Wide Orbit Traffic System Daypart Standards

attributes.name: definition_logic
attributes.description: The rule-based or SQL/JSON expression that defines segment membership criteria as implemented in Adobe AEP or Nielsen. Captures the inclusion/exclusion logic (e.g., age range, viewing frequency thresholds, content genre affinity, platform usage) used to qualify audience members into this segment.
attributes.references: Adobe Experience Platform Segment Builder; Nielsen Audience Workbench

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: The date from which this segment definition is considered valid and available for business use. Segments may be pre-built ahead of upfront sales seasons or campaign launches. Enables temporal validity management for segment versioning and historical reporting.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Internal Data Governance Standards; IAB Audience Data Lifecycle

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: The date after which this segment definition is no longer valid for new activations. Null indicates an open-ended segment with no planned expiry. Used to manage seasonal segments (e.g., sweeps-period segments), campaign-specific segments, and segments tied to expiring data licensing agreements.
attributes.references: Media Broadcasting Internal Data Governance Standards; IAB Audience Data Lifecycle

attributes.name: estimated_reach
attributes.description: Estimated number of unique individuals (persons or households) who qualify for this segment at the time of last refresh. Reach is a core Nielsen and IAB metric used in ad sales proposals, GRP/TRP calculations, and CPM pricing. Distinct from impressions — counts unique audience members, not exposures.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Audience Measurement Standards; IAB Reach and Frequency Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: estimated_reach_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the estimated_reach figure. 'persons' aligns with Nielsen PUT (Persons Using Television) methodology; 'households' aligns with HUT (Homes Using Television); 'devices' applies to digital/OTT platform segments measured by device-level identity.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research HUT/PUT Measurement Standards; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: gender_target
attributes.description: Gender composition target for the segment as defined in Nielsen demographic cells and ad sales targeting parameters. 'all' indicates gender-neutral targeting. Used in GRP (Gross Rating Point) and TRP (Target Rating Point) calculations for ad campaign planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Demographic Standards; IAB Audience Taxonomy

attributes.name: grp_index
attributes.description: The GRP (Gross Rating Point) index value representing this segment's relative audience weight as a percentage of the total universe. GRP is a fundamental media planning metric equal to Reach × Frequency. Used in upfront and scatter market ad sales to price inventory and measure campaign delivery against this segment.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research GRP Methodology; IAB Audience Measurement Guidelines

attributes.name: hut_put_basis
attributes.description: Indicates whether the segment's reach and rating metrics are calculated on a HUT (Homes Using Television) or PUT (Persons Using Television) basis. HUT is household-level measurement; PUT is person-level. This distinction governs how GRP/TRP values are interpreted and how the segment is applied in Nielsen-based ad sales planning.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research HUT/PUT Methodology Standards

attributes.name: income_bracket
attributes.description: Household income tier associated with the segment's demographic composition, used in premium ad targeting and CPM (Cost Per Mille) pricing. Expressed as a standardized range label (e.g., '$75K-$100K HHI', '$100K+ HHI'). Sourced from Nielsen MRI-Simmons or first-party subscriber data. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: under_25k|25k_50k|50k_75k|75k_100k|100k_150k|150k_plus — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: is_dai_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment is approved and technically configured for use in DAI (Dynamic Ad Insertion) workflows on OTT and streaming platforms. DAI-eligible segments can be activated in real-time ad decisioning systems integrated with Akamai CDN and programmatic ad servers for addressable advertising.
attributes.references: SCTE-130 Dynamic Ad Insertion Standard; IAB VAST/VMAP Standards; Akamai DAI Integration

attributes.name: is_sweeps_validated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment's reach and demographic composition estimates have been validated using Nielsen Sweeps period data (the intensive ratings measurement periods in February, May, July, and November). Sweeps-validated segments carry higher confidence for upfront ad sales commitments and programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Sweeps Methodology; FCC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: last_refresh_timestamp

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: nielsen_segment_code

attributes.name: notes

attributes.name: segment_category

attributes.name: segment_code

attributes.name: segment_description

attributes.name: segment_name

attributes.name: segment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the segment by the primary methodology used to define it. attributes.name: trp_index
attributes.description: The TRP (Target Rating Point) index value representing this segment's rating within its specific target demographic universe. attributes.name: version_number

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Cross-platform measurement requires specialized analysts to perform deduplication, validate MRC-accredited methodologies, reconcile linear/OTT/MVPD impressions, and certify total audience metrics. Ana

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Cross-platform audience drives profit center revenue allocation across distribution channels. Segment reporting for investors and internal management reviews require tying total audience delivery to n

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to audience.sweeps_period. Business justification: Cross-platform measurements during sweeps periods are critical for upfront negotiations and guarantee reconciliation. The is_sweeps_period flag indicates relevance, but the specific sweeps period shou

attributes.name: audience_share
attributes.description: Percentage of the total viewing audience (HUT or PUT) that was watching this specific content or channel during the measurement period. Calculated as the program rating divided by HUT or PUT. Key programming performance indicator.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: average_frequency
attributes.description: Average number of times a unique individual in the deduplicated reach was exposed to the content or campaign across all platforms within the measurement period. Calculated as total impressions divided by deduplicated reach.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards; IAB Frequency Standards

attributes.name: co_viewing_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Multiplicative adjustment factor applied to account for co-viewing behavior (multiple persons watching on a single device/screen), particularly relevant for connected TV and OTT platforms. Values greater than 1.0 indicate upward adjustment for co-viewing. Sourced from Nielsen co-viewing methodology.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE Co-Viewing Methodology; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards

attributes.name: content_genre
attributes.description: Genre classification of the content title being measured (e.g., Drama, News, Sports, Reality, Comedy, Documentary). Used for audience segmentation analysis and programming strategy reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: drama|news|sports|reality|comedy|documentary|talk|game_show|animation|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Dalet Galaxy MAM; EIDR Content Classification; Motion Picture Association (MPA)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this cross-platform measurement record was first ingested into the Silver layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: cross_platform_grp
attributes.description: Gross Rating Point (GRP) calculated across all measured platforms, representing the sum of ratings for all platform exposures within the target universe. Equals total impressions divided by the target universe population, multiplied by 100. Primary audience currency for converged TV ad buying.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards; IAB GRP Standards

attributes.name: cross_platform_trp
attributes.description: Target Rating Point (TRP) calculated across all measured platforms for the specified target demographic segment. Measures GRP within the defined target audience, used for demographic-specific ad buying and campaign performance evaluation.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards; IAB TRP Standards

attributes.name: currency_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the audience measurement currency standard applied to this record (e.g., 'Nielsen ONE v2.1', 'Comscore Campaign Ratings v3.0'). Supports multi-currency and currency transition tracking as the industry evolves from legacy Nielsen C3/C7 to cross-platform currencies.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards; IAB Cross-Platform Currency

attributes.name: data_source_systems
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of operational source systems that contributed data to this cross-platform measurement record (e.g., 'Nielsen Media Research Platform|Adobe Experience Platform'). Supports data lineage, audit, and methodology transparency requirements.
attributes.references: MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards; SOX Section 404; Internal Data Lineage Policy

attributes.name: daypart_code

attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; IAB Daypart Standards; ATSC

attributes.name: deduplicated_reach
attributes.description: Total count of unique, unduplicated individuals (persons) who were exposed to the content or campaign across all measured platforms within the measurement period. Core audience currency metric for converged TV buying. Expressed as absolute person count.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards; IAB Cross-Platform Measurement

attributes.name: distribution_type
attributes.description: Primary distribution model classification for the content being measured: 'linear' for traditional scheduled broadcast; 'vod' for generic on-demand; 'svod' for subscription streaming; 'avod' for ad-supported streaming; 'tvod' for transactional on-demand; 'fast' for free ad-supported streaming TV; 'social' for social video platforms. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: linear|vod|svod|avod|tvod|fast|social — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines; Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Standards

attributes.name: fast_channel_impressions
attributes.description: Audience impressions attributed to Free Ad-Supported Streaming Television (FAST) channels within the measurement period. Represents the growing ad-supported streaming audience segment.
attributes.references: IAB FAST Channel Measurement Guidelines; Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Standards

attributes.name: hut_rating
attributes.description: Homes Using Television (HUT) rating for the measurement period, representing the percentage of all television households with at least one TV set in use during the measured time period. Used for share calculations and programming decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: is_data_suppressed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this measurement record has been suppressed from reporting due to insufficient panel sample size, MRC minimum reporting thresholds, or privacy regulations (GDPR/CCPA). Suppressed records are retained for audit but excluded from audience currency reporting.
attributes.references: MRC Minimum Reporting Standards; GDPR Article 5; CCPA Section 1798.100

attributes.name: is_mrc_accredited
attributes.description: Indicates whether this measurement was produced using a methodology that holds current Media Rating Council (MRC) accreditation for cross-platform measurement. MRC accreditation is required for use as official audience currency in upfront and scatter market ad transactions.

attributes.name: is_sweeps_period
attributes.description: Indicates whether this measurement falls within a Nielsen sweeps period (February, May, July, November), which represents an intensive ratings measurement window used for programming and ad rate decisions.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; Nielsen Sweeps Methodology

attributes.name: isan_code
attributes.description: International Standard Audiovisual Number (ISAN) for the content title being measured, providing a globally unique, persistent identifier for the audiovisual work. Enables cross-system content identification and rights reconciliation.
attributes.references: ISO 15706 ISAN Standard; EIDR; Motion Picture Association (MPA)

attributes.name: linear_impressions
attributes.description: Audience impressions attributed to traditional linear broadcast television (over-the-air, cable, satellite) within the measurement period. Component of the platform-level audience breakdown.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; ATSC; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: measurement_period_end
attributes.description: The last date of the audience measurement observation window, aligned to the content airing schedule or campaign flight end.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: measurement_period_start
attributes.description: The first date of the audience measurement observation window, aligned to the content airing schedule or campaign flight start. Used for sweeps period identification and daypart analysis.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: measurement_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this cross-platform measurement record, used in reporting, ad sales proposals, and audience currency reconciliation. Sourced from Nielsen Media Research Platform or internal measurement workflow.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards

attributes.name: measurement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the cross-platform measurement record. 'draft' indicates data is being assembled; 'preliminary' indicates initial estimate released; 'certified' indicates MRC-audited final figure; 'revised' indicates a post-certification correction; 'archived' indicates superseded by a newer measurement.
attributes.references: MRC Cross-Platform Measurement Standards; Nielsen ONE Certification Process

attributes.name: measurement_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal real-world timestamp representing when the audience measurement observation period was captured or the measurement run was executed. Distinct from record audit timestamps.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: mvpd_impressions
attributes.description: Audience impressions attributed to Multichannel Video Programming Distributor (MVPD) and virtual MVPD (vMVPD) platforms, including cable, satellite, and virtual pay-TV providers within the measurement period.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; SCTE Standards; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: nielsen_rating
attributes.description: The Nielsen Rating for the content or program within the measurement period, representing the percentage of all television households or persons in the universe tuned to the program. The foundational audience currency metric for linear broadcast.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: ott_streaming_impressions
attributes.description: Audience impressions attributed to Over-The-Top (OTT) and Subscription Video On Demand (SVOD) streaming platforms within the measurement period. Includes authenticated streaming on connected TV, mobile, and desktop devices.
attributes.references: Nielsen ONE; IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines; MRC Cross-Platform Standards

attributes.name: panel_sample_size
attributes.description: Number of panel households or persons in the Nielsen (or equivalent vendor) measurement panel that contributed to this cross-platform measurement. Indicates statistical reliability; low sample sizes may trigger data suppression per MRC minimum reporting standards.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Minimum Reporting Standards

attributes.name: put_rating
attributes.description: Persons Using Television (PUT) rating for the measurement period, representing the percentage of all persons in the universe who are watching television during the measured time period. Used for person-level audience share calculations.
attributes.references: Nielsen Media Research Platform; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: social_video_impressions
attributes.description: Audience impressions attributed to social video platforms (e.g., YouTube, Facebook Video, TikTok, Instagram Reels) within the measurement period. Enables full cross-platform audience aggregation.
attributes.references: IAB Digital Video Measurement Guidelines; Nielsen ONE; MRC Cross-Platform Standards

attributes.name: target_universe_size
attributes.description: The estimated total population size of the target demographic universe used as the denominator for GRP and TRP calculations. Sourced from Nielsen universe estimates updated annually.
attributes.references: Nielsen Universe Estimates; MRC Audience Measurement Standards

attributes.name: total_impressions
attributes.description: Total number of audience exposures (impressions) across all platforms within the measurement period, including duplicate exposures across platforms. Used for CPM-based advertising currency and GRP calculation inputs.
attributes.references: IAB Impression Measurement Guidelines; MRC Viewability Standards; Nielsen ONE

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this cross-platform measurement record was last modified, supporting data lineage and revision tracking.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; Internal Data Governance Policy

products.name: market_distribution_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the contractual distribution agreement between a market coverage area and a distribution partner. It captures market-specific carriage terms, subscriber economics, and territorial rights that exist only in the context of this market-partner relationship. Each record links one DMA/market to one distribution partner with commercial terms, performance metrics, and exclusivity provisions that vary by market-partner combination.. Existence Justification: Distribution partners (MVPDs, vMVPDs, affiliates, syndicators) operate across multiple geographic markets, each with market-specific carriage agreements, subscriber counts, and commercial terms. Conversely, each DMA/market has multiple distribution partners competing or coexisting with different penetration rates, carriage fees, and exclusivity provisions. This is the operational foundation of territorial rights management and market-based distribution economics in media broadcasting.

attributes.name: market_distribution_agreement_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this market-partner distribution agreement record

attributes.name: market_coverage_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Market Distribution Agreement - Market Coverage Id

attributes.name: partner_id

attributes.name: agreement_status

attributes.name: carriage_fee_per_subscriber
attributes.description: Negotiated monthly or annual fee paid per subscriber for carriage rights in this specific market. This rate varies by market size, partner type, and competitive dynamics.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this market-specific distribution agreement expires or terminates. Null indicates an evergreen or currently active agreement.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this market-specific distribution agreement becomes effective and carriage rights commence.

attributes.name: exclusivity_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this distribution agreement grants exclusive carriage rights to the partner in this market, preventing competing distribution deals.

attributes.name: last_renewal_date
attributes.description: Date when this market-specific agreement was most recently renewed or renegotiated.

attributes.name: must_carry_status
attributes.description: FCC regulatory classification for this market-partner carriage relationship: must-carry obligation, retransmission consent negotiation, or not applicable.

attributes.name: next_negotiation_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next contract renegotiation or renewal discussion for this market-partner relationship.

attributes.name: penetration_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of total TV households in the market that subscribe to this partner's service. Calculated as subscriber_count divided by market TV household universe.

attributes.name: performance_tier
attributes.description: Classification of the partner's performance in this specific market based on subscriber growth, payment compliance, and audience delivery metrics.

attributes.name: retransmission_consent_granted
attributes.description: Indicates whether retransmission consent has been granted to this partner for broadcast signals in this market, per FCC regulations.

attributes.name: subscriber_count
attributes.description: Current number of subscribers the partner serves in this market. Used to calculate total carriage fees and assess market penetration.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this market distribution agreement record was last modified.

products.name: talent_demographic_appeal
products.description: This association product represents the measured appeal and awareness metrics of talent across specific demographic segments. It captures Q Score ratings, awareness percentages, favorability ratings, and appeal indices that exist only in the context of a specific talent-demographic combination. Each record links one talent_profile to one demographic_segment with measurement data used for casting decisions, talent booking, programming strategy, and advertising sales targeting. This is the operational system of record for talent appeal research used by programming, casting, and ad sales teams.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting operations, talent appeal is measured across multiple demographic segments simultaneously (e.g., a host has different Q Scores for A18-49, W25-54, M18-34), and each demographic segment has appeal measurements for multiple talent profiles. Casting directors, programming strategists, and ad sales teams actively query and manage this appeal data to make talent booking decisions, programming placement, and advertising targeting decisions. This is operational audience research data, not an analytical correlation.

attributes.name: casting_recommendation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this talent is recommended for casting in content targeting this demographic segment based on appeal thresholds. Used by casting directors and programming teams.

attributes.name: confidence_interval
attributes.description: Statistical confidence interval (margin of error) for the appeal metrics in this measurement, expressed as a percentage. Used to assess measurement precision.

attributes.name: favorability_rating

attributes.name: measurement_vendor
attributes.description: The research vendor or organization that conducted the appeal measurement (e.g., Marketing Evaluations Inc., Nielsen, custom internal research). Used for data provenance and methodology validation.

attributes.name: q_score
attributes.description: The Marketing Evaluations Q Score for this talent within this demographic segment. Measures familiarity and appeal, used industry-wide for talent valuation and casting decisions.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: sample_size

products.name: partner_demographic_target
products.description: This association product represents the contractual audience targeting agreement between partners and demographic segments. It captures partner-specific demographic targeting strategies where each partner (advertiser, agency, network) negotiates specific performance guarantees, CPM rates, and priority levels for each demographic segment they target. Each record links one partner to one demographic segment with commercial terms that exist only in the context of this business relationship.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting operations, partners (advertisers, agencies, networks) negotiate targeting agreements for multiple demographic segments simultaneously, each with distinct CPM rates, performance guarantees, and priority levels. Conversely, each demographic segment (e.g., A18-49, W25-54) is targeted by multiple partners with varying commercial terms. Media sales teams actively manage these partner-demographic targeting agreements as contractual commitments that drive inventory allocation, pricing, and make-good obligations.

attributes.name: partner_demographic_target_id

attributes.name: demographic_segment_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Partner Demographic Target - Demographic Segment Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the demographic segment being targeted in this partner agreement

attributes.name: partner_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Partner Demographic Target - Partner Partner Partner Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the partner who is targeting this demographic segment

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this partner demographic targeting agreement expires or is superseded. Null indicates an ongoing evergreen agreement.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this partner demographic targeting agreement becomes active. Aligns with contract effective dates or campaign flight dates.

attributes.name: guaranteed_rating

products.name: segment_regulatory_compliance
products.description: This association product represents the compliance relationship between audience segments and regulatory obligations. It captures the activation compliance status, audit history, and risk assessment for each segment-obligation pairing. Each record links one audience segment to one regulatory obligation with attributes that track when the segment was activated under that obligation, its current compliance state, audit findings, and any exemptions or special handling requirements.. Existence Justification: In media broadcasting operations, audience segments are subject to multiple regulatory obligations simultaneously (COPPA for children's content, GDPR for EU audiences, accessibility requirements, advertising restrictions), and each regulatory obligation governs multiple audience segments across the portfolio. The compliance team actively manages these relationships by tracking activation dates, conducting periodic audits, assessing risk levels specific to each segment-obligation pairing, documenting exemptions, and maintaining remediation plans. This is an operational compliance management process, not an analytical correlation.

attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for this segment-obligation compliance record. Primary key.
